And We have fixed their number (19) only as a trial for the disbelievers, in order that the people of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) may arrive at a certainty [that this Qur’ân is the truth as it agrees with their Books regarding the number (19) which is written in the Taurât (Torah) and the Injeel (Gospel)] and that the believers may increase in Faith (as this Qur’ân is the truth), and that no doubt may be left for the people of the Scripture and the believers, and that those in whose hearts is a disease (of hypocrisy) and the disbelievers may say: "What Allâh intends by this (curious) example ?" Thus Allâh leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And none can know the hosts of your Lord but He. And this (Hell) is nothing else than a (warning) reminder to mankind.

metadata.arabic: كَلاَّ وَٱلْقَمَرِ
metadata.Tafsir: (Nay, by the Moon) Allah swore by the moon

translation: Nay! And by the moon

metadata.arabic: وَٱللَّيْلِ إِذْ أَدْبَرَ
metadata.Tafsir: (And the night when it withdraweth

translation: And by the night when it withdraws.

metadata.arabic: وَٱلصُّبْحِ إِذَآ أَسْفَرَ
metadata.Tafsir: And the dawn when it shineth forth.

translation: And by the dawn when it brightens.

metadata.arabic: إِنَّهَا لإِحْدَى ٱلْكُبَرِ
metadata.Tafsir: Lo! this is) i.e. Saqar (one of the greatest (portents)) this is one of the gates of the Fire; other gates include: Jahannam, Laza, al-Hutamah, al-Sa'ir, al-Jahim, and al-Hawiyah.

translation: Verily, it (Hell, or their denial of Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم, or the Day of Resurrection) is but one of the greatest (signs).

metadata.arabic: نَذِيراً لِّلْبَشَرِ
metadata.Tafsir: (As a warning unto men) it is also said this means: Muhammad (pbuh) is a warner unto mankind. This leads us to the beginning of the surah and Allah's saying (Arise and warn), this latter part being mentioned last when it is the first part of the sequence,

translation: A warning to mankind -

metadata.arabic: لِمَن شَآءَ مِنكُمْ أَن يَتَقَدَّمَ أَوْ يَتَأَخَّرَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Unto him of you who will advance) towards goodness (or hang back) from evil and therefore holds back from it; it is also said this means: or hang back from goodness and therefore disbelieve; this being a threat to them.

translation: To any of you that chooses to go forward (by working righteous deeds), or to remain behind (by committing sins).

metadata.arabic: كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ رَهِينَةٌ
metadata.Tafsir: (Every soul) every disbelieving soul (is a pledge) in the Fire for eternity (for its own deeds) which it has earned in its state of disbelief;

translation: Every person is a pledge for what he has earned,

metadata.arabic: إِلاَّ أَصْحَابَ ٱلْيَمِينِ
metadata.Tafsir: (Save these who will stand on the right hand) who are the dwellers of Paradise who are not the same.

translation: Except those on the Right, (i.e. the pious true believers of Islâmic Monotheism).

metadata.arabic: فِي جَنَّاتٍ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ
metadata.Tafsir: Rather, they are (In Gardens they will ask one another

translation: In Gardens (Paradise) they will ask one another,

metadata.arabic: عَنِ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ
metadata.Tafsir: Concerning the guilty) they will ask the dwellers of the Fire:

translation: About Al-Mujrimûn (polytheists, criminals, disbelievers), (And they will say to them):

metadata.arabic: مَا سَلَكَكُمْ فِي سَقَرَ
metadata.Tafsir: O so-and-so (What hath brought you to this burning?

translation: "What has caused you to enter Hell?"

metadata.arabic: قَالُواْ لَمْ نَكُ مِنَ ٱلْمُصَلِّينَ
metadata.Tafsir: They will answer) the dwellers of the Fire will answer: (We were not of those who prayed) the five daily prayers, i.e. we were not among the Muslims.

translation: They will say: "We were not of those who used to offer the Salât (prayers),

metadata.arabic: وَلَمْ نَكُ نُطْعِمُ ٱلْمِسْكِينَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Nor did we feed the wretched) we did not encourage giving alms to the needy nor were we among those who gave the poor-due or alms.

translation: "Nor we used to feed Al-Miskîn (the poor);

metadata.arabic: وَكُنَّا نَخُوضُ مَعَ ٱلُخَآئِضِينَ
metadata.Tafsir: (We used to wade (in vain dispute) with (all) waders) we used to indulge with the adherents of falsehood,

translation: "And we used to talk falsehood (all that which Allâh hated) with vain talkers.

metadata.arabic: وَكُنَّا نُكَذِّبُ بِيَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ
metadata.Tafsir: (And we used to deny the Day of Judgement) and we used to say that the Day of Reckoning will never happen,

translation: And we used to belie the Day of Recompense,

metadata.arabic: حَتَّىٰ أَتَانَا ٱلْيَقِينُ
metadata.Tafsir: (Till the inevitable came unto us) until death came to us.

translation: "Until there came to us (the death) that is certain."

metadata.arabic: فَمَا تَنفَعُهُمْ شَفَاعَةُ ٱلشَّافِعِينَ
metadata.Tafsir: (The mediation of no mediators will avail them then) Allah says: the intercession of the angels, prophets and righteous ones will not benefit them.

translation: So no intercession of intercessors will be of any use to them.

metadata.arabic: فَمَا لَهُمْ عَنِ ٱلتَّذْكِرَةِ مُعْرِضِينَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Why now turn they away from) disbelieve in (the Admonishment) the Qur'an

translation: Then what is wrong with them (i.e. the polytheists, the disbelievers) that they turn away from (receiving) admonition?

metadata.arabic: كَأَنَّهُمْ حُمُرٌ مُّسْتَنفِرَةٌ
metadata.Tafsir: (As they were frightened asses

translation: As if they were (frightened) wild donkeys.

metadata.arabic: فَرَّتْ مِن قَسْوَرَةٍ
metadata.Tafsir: Fleeing from a lion) and it is said: from marksmen: and it is said: from a group of men?

translation: Fleeing from a hunter, or a lion, or a beast of prey.

metadata.arabic: بَلْ يُرِيدُ كُلُّ ٱمْرِىءٍ مِّنْهُمْ أَن يُؤْتَىٰ صُحُفاً مُّنَشَّرَةً
metadata.Tafsir: (Nay, but everyone of them desireth that he should be given open pages (from Allah)) a book wherein is written his crimes and repentance, for they said: “bring us a book in which is written our crimes and repentance and we will believe in you”.

translation: Nay, everyone of them desires that he should be given pages spread out (coming from Allâh with a writing that Islâm is the right religion, and Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم has come with the truth from Allâh, the Lord of the heavens and earth).

metadata.arabic: كَلاَّ بَل لاَّ يَخَافُونَ ٱلآخِرَةَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Nay, verily) he will not be given this. (They fear not the Hereafter) they do not fear the torment of the Hereafter.

translation: Nay! But they fear not the Hereafter (from Allâh’s punishment).

metadata.arabic: كَلاَّ إِنَّهُ تَذْكِرَةٌ
metadata.Tafsir: (Nay, verily) O Muhammad. (Lo! this is an Admonishment) whoever wishes to take admonition from the Qur'an, will be admonished.

translation: Nay, verily, this (Qur’an) is an admonition,

metadata.arabic: فَمَن شَآءَ ذَكَرَهُ
metadata.Tafsir: (So whosoever will may heed) may take admonition.

translation: So whosoever will (let him read it), and receive admonition (from it)!

metadata.arabic: وَمَا يَذْكُرُونَ إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ هُوَ أَهْلُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ وَأَهْلُ ٱلْمَغْفِرَةِ
metadata.Tafsir: (And they will not heed unless Allah willeth (it). He is the fount of fear) He deserves to be feared such that He is not disobeyed. (He is the fount of Mercy) He is capable of forgiving those who repent, for He is the possessor of forgiveness when the Day of Resurrection takes place'.

translation: And they will not receive admonition unless Allâh wills; He (Allâh) is the One, deserving that mankind should be afraid of, and should be dutiful to Him, and should not take any Ilâh (god) along with Him, and He is the One Who forgives (sins).

metadata.arabic: لاَ أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said concerning the interpretation of Allah's (Nay, I swear by the Day of Resurrection): '(Nay, I swear by the Day of Resurrection) He says: I swear that the Day of Resurrection will happen;

translation: I swear by the Day of Resurrection.

metadata.arabic: وَلاَ أُقْسِمُ بِٱلنَّفْسِ ٱللَّوَّامَةِ
metadata.Tafsir: (Nay, I swear by the accusing soul (that this Scripture is true)) and I swear by every righteous and sinful soul that will blame itself on the Day of Resurrection. As for the righteous soul, it will say: if only I did more righteous works. And as for the sinful soul, it will say: if only I abstained from committing sins. Both souls will say this upon seeing the reward and punishment awaiting each one of them respectively. It is also said that the accusing soul in question is the soul that reproaches itself; and it is also said: it is the soul that repents of its sins and reproaches itself for what it had committed; and it is also said it is the sinful, disbelieving soul.

translation: And I swear by the self-reproaching person (a believer).

metadata.arabic: أَيَحْسَبُ ٱلإِنسَانُ أَلَّن نَّجْمَعَ عِظَامَهُ
metadata.Tafsir: (Thinketh man) does the disbelieving man, 'Adiyy Ibn Rabi'ah, think because he did not believe in the resurrection (that We shall not assemble his bones) that We are not able to gather his bones after they scatter, change and turn into dust?

translation: Does man (a disbeliever) think that We shall not assemble his bones?

metadata.arabic: بَلَىٰ قَادِرِينَ عَلَىٰ أَن نُّسَوِّيَ بَنَانَهُ
metadata.Tafsir: (Yea, verily) I am capable of doing so. (Yea, We are able to restore his very fingers!) We are able to gather his fingers, such that his palm becomes like the hoof of a camel or beasts. He says: We are able to make his hand look like the hoof of a camel, so how is it that We cannot restore his bones?

translation: Yes, We are Able to put together in perfect order the tips of his fingers.

metadata.arabic: بَلْ يُرِيدُ ٱلإِنسَانُ لِيَفْجُرَ أَمَامَهُ
metadata.Tafsir: (But man) the disbelieving man: 'Adiyy Ibn Rabi'ah (would fain deny what is before him) would fain to indulge in his evil acts and delay his repentance; it is also said this means: he would fain to engage in evil deeds and indecencies in his future days.

translation: Nay! Man (denies Resurrection and Reckoning. So he) desires to continue committing sins.

metadata.arabic: يَسْأَلُ أَيَّانَ يَوْمُ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ
metadata.Tafsir: (He asketh) 'Adiyy Ibn Rabi'ah asks in his denial of the resurrection: (When will be this Day of Resurrection) when will the Day of Resurrection take place?

translation: He asks: "When will be this Day of Resurrection?"

metadata.arabic: فَإِذَا بَرِقَ ٱلْبَصَرُ
metadata.Tafsir: Allah said to him: (But when sight is confounded) and it is also said this means: when sight is pleased

translation: So, when the sight shall be dazed.

metadata.arabic: وَخَسَفَ ٱلْقَمَرُ
metadata.Tafsir: (And the moon is eclipsed) and the light of the moon disappears

translation: And the moon will be eclipsed.

metadata.arabic: وَجُمِعَ ٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ
metadata.Tafsir: (And sun and moon are united) like two black, horned bulls whose hooves are beaten and then are thrown in the veil of light,

translation: And the sun and moon will be joined together (by going one into the other or folded up or deprived of their light).

metadata.arabic: يَقُولُ ٱلإِنسَانُ يَوْمَئِذٍ أَيْنَ ٱلْمَفَرُّ
metadata.Tafsir: (On that day man) the disbelieving man: 'Adiyy Ibn Rabi'ah and his companions (will cry: Whither to flee) from the Fire and take refuse!

translation: On that Day man will say: "Where (is the refuge) to flee?"

metadata.arabic: كَلاَّ لاَ وَزَرَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Alas! No refuge!) Truly, there is no mountain to shield him from the Fire, nor are there any trees, cover, fortress, refuge or safety for them from Allah.

translation: No! There is no refuge!

metadata.arabic: إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ ٱلْمُسْتَقَرُّ
metadata.Tafsir: (Unto thy Lord is the recourse) the return and last resort (that day) the Day of Judgement.

translation: Unto your Lord (Alone) will be the place of rest that Day.

metadata.arabic: يُنَبَّأُ ٱلإِنسَانُ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِمَا قَدَّمَ وَأَخَّرَ
metadata.Tafsir: (On that day) on the Day of Judgement (man is told) 'Adiyy Ibn Rabi'ah and others will be informed about (the tale of that which he hath sent before and left behind) the tale of what he has sent before of good or evil works and of what he left behind of good or evil wont; it is also said this means: he will be informed about what he has sent before of acts of obedience and what he left behind of acts of disobedience.

translation: On that Day man will be informed of what he sent forward (of his evil good deeds), and what he left behind (of his good or evil traditions).

metadata.arabic: بَلِ ٱلإِنسَانُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ بَصِيرَةٌ
metadata.Tafsir: (Oh, but man) 'Adiyy Ibn Rabi'ah and others (is a telling witness against himself) He says: he will testify against his own self,

translation: Nay! Man will be a witness against himself [as his body parts (skin, hands, legs, etc.) will speak about his deeds],

metadata.arabic: وَلَوْ أَلْقَىٰ مَعَاذِيرَهُ
metadata.Tafsir: (Although he tender his excuses) and says: I have not done this and have not said that; it is also said that this means: every soul is aware of the faults of others, ignorant of and oblivious to its own faults.

translation: Though he may put forth his excuses (to cover his evil deeds).

metadata.arabic: لاَ تُحَرِّكْ بِهِ لِسَانَكَ لِتَعْجَلَ بِهِ
metadata.Tafsir: (Stir not thy tongue) to read the Qur'an, O Muhammad, (herewith to hasten it) to hasten the recitation of the Qur'an before Gabriel finishes reciting it to you. This is because the Prophet (pbuh) used to repeat whatever revelations of the Qur'an Gabriel brought down to him before the latter finished a sentence of the Qur'an, out of fear of forgetting what was revealed to him. Allah warned him against doing so.

translation: Move not your tongue concerning (the Qur’ân, O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) to make haste therewith.

metadata.arabic: إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا جَمْعَهُ وَقُرْآنَهُ
metadata.Tafsir: (Lo! upon Us (resteth) the putting together thereof) preserving the Qur'an in your heart (and the reading thereof) and also preserving the reading of Gabriel to you; it is also said that this means: upon Us rests its composition of the lawful and the unlawful.

translation: It is for Us to collect it and to give you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) the ability to recite it (the Qur’ân).

metadata.arabic: فَإِذَا قَرَأْنَاهُ فَٱتَّبِعْ قُرْآنَهُ
metadata.Tafsir: (And when We read it) when Gabriel reads to you, (follow thou the reading) you, O Muhammad, read after him; it is also said this means: what We finish composing it with all the lawful and unlawful contained therein, do you follow its composition;

translation: And when We have recited it to you [O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم through Jibrîl (Gabriel)], then follow its (the Qur’an’s) recital.

metadata.arabic: ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا بَيَانَهُ
metadata.Tafsir: (Then lo! upon Us (resteth) the explanation thereof) the explanation of the lawful and unlawful, the commands and prohibitions.

translation: Then it is for Us (Allâh) to make it clear (to you).

metadata.arabic: كَلاَّ بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Nay) truly, (but ye do love the fleeting Now) working for the life of the world

translation: Not [as you think, that you (mankind) will not be resurrected and recompensed for your deeds], but you (men) love the present life of this world,

metadata.arabic: وَتَذَرُونَ ٱلآخِرَةَ
metadata.Tafsir: (And neglect the Hereafter) and neglect working for the reward of the Hereafter.

translation: And neglect the Hereafter.

metadata.arabic: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَّاضِرَةٌ
metadata.Tafsir: (That day) the Day of Judgement (will faces) the faces of the believers who are true in their faith (be resplendent) beautiful, seemly and tender,

translation: Some faces that Day shall be Nâdirah (shining and radiant).

metadata.arabic: إِلَىٰ رَبِّهَا نَاظِرَةٌ
metadata.Tafsir: (Looking towards their Lord) they behold the Countenance of their Lord and are not veiled from Him;

translation: Looking at their Lord (Allâh).

metadata.arabic: وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ بَاسِرَةٌ
metadata.Tafsir: (And that day) the Day of Judgement (will other faces) the faces of the disbelievers and hypocrites (be despondent) gloomy; veiled from seeing their Lord,

translation: And some faces, that Day, will be Bâsirah (dark, gloomy, frowning, and sad),

metadata.arabic: تَظُنُّ أَن يُفْعَلَ بِهَا فَاقِرَةٌ
metadata.Tafsir: (Thou wilt know) those faces will know (that some great disaster is about to fall on them) a severe and horrible punishment is about to befall them.

translation: Thinking that some calamity is about to fall on them.

metadata.arabic: كَلاَّ إِذَا بَلَغَتِ ٱلتَّرَاقِيَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Nay) truly, (but when the life cometh up to the throat) when the soul of the body reaches the throat

translation: Nay, when (the soul) reaches to the collar bone (i.e. up to the throat in its exit),

metadata.arabic: وَقِيلَ مَنْ رَاقٍ
metadata.Tafsir: (And men say) and those around it among his family and others say: (Where is the wizard (who can save him now)?) Is there any physician who can cure him? It is also said this means: the angels say to one another: who will rise with his soul to Allah?

translation: And it will be said: "Who can cure him (and save him from death)?"

metadata.arabic: وَظَنَّ أَنَّهُ ٱلْفِرَاقُ
metadata.Tafsir: (And he knowth) and the dead person knows at that point (that it is the parting) the time of departing from the life of the world;

translation: And he (the dying person) will conclude that it was (the time) of parting (death);

metadata.arabic: وَٱلْتَفَّتِ ٱلسَّاقُ بِٱلسَّاقِ
metadata.Tafsir: (And agony is heaped on agony) and severity is heaped upon severity: the severity of the last day of the life of the world and that of the first day of the Hereafter; and it is also said this means: and the dead person's legs are twisted around each other;

translation: And one leg will be joined with another leg (shrouded).

metadata.arabic: إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ ٱلْمَسَاقُ
metadata.Tafsir: (Unto thy Lord that day) the Day of Judgement (will be the driving) the return of all created beings.

translation: The drive will be, on that Day, to your Lord (Allâh)!

metadata.arabic: فَلاَ صَدَّقَ وَلاَ صَلَّىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (For he) i.e. Abu Jahl (neither trusted) neither believed in Allah's divine Oneness, (nor prayed) nor embraced Islam and became of those who perform the prayer.

translation: So he (the disbeliever) neither believed (in this Qur’ân and in the Message of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) nor prayed!

metadata.arabic: وَلَـٰكِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (But he denied) Allah's divine Oneness (and flouted) and turned away from faith.

translation: But on the contrary, he belied (this Qur’ân and the Message of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) and turned away!

metadata.arabic: ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِ يَتَمَطَّىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Then went he to his folk) in the life of the world (with glee) strutting and behaving wantonly.

translation: Then he walked in conceit (full pride) to his family admiring himself!

metadata.arabic: أَوْلَىٰ لَكَ فَأَوْلَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: The Prophet (pbuh) received him, grabbed him and shook him once or twice and then said: (Nearer unto thee and nearer) this is a threat to you, O Abu Jahl, it is indeed a threat.

translation: Woe to you [O man (disbeliever)]! And then (again) woe to you!

metadata.arabic: ثُمَّ أَوْلَىٰ لَكَ فَأَوْلَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Again nearer unto thee and nearer (is the doom)) beware, O Abu Jahl.

translation: Again, woe to you [O man (disbeliever)]! And then (again) woe to you!

metadata.arabic: أَيَحْسَبُ ٱلإِنسَانُ أَن يُتْرَكَ سُدًى
metadata.Tafsir: The Qur'an also said: (Thinks man) the disbelieving man, i.e. Abu Jahl (that he is to be left aimless) neglected, without any commands, prohibitions or admonition?

translation: Does man think that he will be left neglected (without being punished or rewarded for the obligatory duties enjoined by his Lord Allâh on him)?

metadata.arabic: أَلَمْ يَكُ نُطْفَةً مِّن مَّنِيٍّ يُمْنَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Was he not) i.e. Abu Jahl (a drop of fluid) man's sperm drops (which gushed forth) in the woman's womb; and it is also said: created in the woman's womb?

translation: Was he not a Nutfah (mixed male and female sexual discharge) of semen emitted (poured forth)?

metadata.arabic: ثُمَّ كَانَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Then he became a clot) then he became clotted blood; (then (Allah) shaped) him a living being (and fashioned) him with two hands, two feet, two eyes, two ears as well as with all the other members, and also placed in him the spirit.

translation: Then he became an ‘Alaqah (a clot); then (Allâh) shaped and fashioned (him) in due proportion.

metadata.arabic: فَجَعَلَ مِنْهُ ٱلزَّوْجَيْنِ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلأُنثَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (And made of him) after that (a pair, the male and female) Abu Jahl had a son called 'Ikrimah Ibn Abi Jahl and a daughter called Juwayrah Bint Abi Jahl.

translation: And made of him two sexes, male and female.

metadata.arabic: أَلَيْسَ ذَلِكَ بِقَادِرٍ عَلَىٰ أَن يُحْيِـيَ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Is not He (who doeth so) able to bring the dead to life) for the resurrection? Indeed, our Lord is Able to do so; He is Able to bring the dead back to life just as He did create Adam from dust'.

translation: Is not He (Allâh Who does that) Able to give life to the dead? (Yes! He is Able to do all things).

metadata.arabic: هَلْ أَتَىٰ عَلَى ٱلإِنسَانِ حِينٌ مِّنَ ٱلدَّهْرِ لَمْ يَكُن شَيْئاً مَّذْكُوراً
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (Hath there come upon man (ever)): '(Hath there come upon man (ever)) there has come upon Adam (any period of time) a period of 40 years when he was created and fashioned (in which he was a thing unremembered?) not knowing who he was, what his name was or what Allah wanted from him.

translation: Has there not been over man a period of time, when he was not a thing worth mentioning?

metadata.arabic: إِنَّا خَلَقْنَا ٱلإِنسَانَ مِن نُّطْفَةٍ أَمْشَاجٍ نَّبْتَلِيهِ فَجَعَلْنَاهُ سَمِيعاً بَصِيراً
metadata.Tafsir: (Lo! We create man) i.e. the progeny of Adam (from a drop of thickened fluid) from Adam and Eve's drops of two different kinds of fluid: that of man being white and thick and that of the woman being yellow and thin; thus progeny comes from both of them (to test him) with hardship and comfort; it is also said this means: to test him with good and evil; (so We make him hearing, knowing) We gave him the faculty of hearing so that he could hear the Truth and guidance and the faculty of sight so that he could see the Truth and guidance. It is also said that We make him hearing, knowing in order to test him with good and evil, faith and disbelief.

translation: Verily, We have created man from Nutfah (drops) of mixed semen (sexual discharge of man and woman), in order to try him: so We made him hearer and seer.

metadata.arabic: إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ ٱلسَّبِيلَ إِمَّا شَاكِراً وَإِمَّا كَفُوراً
metadata.Tafsir: (Lo! We have shown him the way) of faith and disbelief, good and evil, (whether he be grateful) accepting faith (or disbelieving) it is also said this means: We have shown him the way to be either grateful or ungrateful.

translation: Verily, We showed him the way, whether he be grateful or ungrateful.

metadata.arabic: إِنَّآ أَعْتَدْنَا لِلْكَافِرِينَ سَلاَسِلاَ وَأَغْلاَلاً وَسَعِيراً
metadata.Tafsir: (Lo! We have prepared for disbelievers) Abu Jahl and his followers (manacles and carcans) in the Fire (and a raging fire.

translation: Verily, We have prepared for the disbelievers iron chains, iron collars, and a blazing Fire.

metadata.arabic: إِنَّ ٱلأَبْرَارَ يَشْرَبُونَ مِن كَأْسٍ كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا كَافُوراً
metadata.Tafsir: Lo! the righteous) who are true in their faith and obey Allah (shall drink of a cup) shall drink wine in Paradise (whereof the mixture is of water of Kafur,

translation: Verily,, the Abrâr (the pious believers of Islamic Monotheism), shall drink of a cup (of wine) mixed with (water from a spring in Paradise called) Kâfûr

metadata.arabic: عَيْناً يَشْرَبُ بِهَا عِبَادُ ٱللَّهِ يُفَجِّرُونَهَا تَفْجِيراً
metadata.Tafsir: A spring wherefrom the slaves of Allah) the friends of Allah (drink, making it gush forth abundantly) whenever they wish, from the Garden into their own habitations and palaces; it is also said that this means: they make it into a mixture;

translation: A spring wherefrom the slaves of Allâh will drink, causing it to gush forth abundantly.

metadata.arabic: يُوفُونَ بِٱلنَّذْرِ وَيَخَافُونَ يَوْماً كَانَ شَرُّهُ مُسْتَطِيراً
metadata.Tafsir: Allah then described their traits when they were in the life of the world, saying: (Because they perform the vow) because they fulfil their pledges and oath by Allah; it is also said this means: they perform the obligations (and fear a day) and fear the torment of a day (whereof the evil) the torment (is wide spreading,

translation: They (are those who) fulfil (their) vows, and they fear a Day whose evil will be wide-spreading.

metadata.arabic: وَيُطْعِمُونَ ٱلطَّعَامَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِ مِسْكِيناً وَيَتِيماً وَأَسِيراً
metadata.Tafsir: And feed with food the needy wretch, the orphan) among the Muslims (and the prisoner) and the Muslim prisoner in the captivity of the idolaters; and it is also said: any kind of prisoner, (for love of Him) despite their desire for food and its scarcity,

translation: And they give food, inspite of their love for it (or for the love of Him), to the Miskîn (the poor), the orphan, and the captive

metadata.arabic: إِنَّمَا نُطْعِمُكُمْ لِوَجْهِ ٱللَّهِ لاَ نُرِيدُ مِنكُمْ جَزَآءً وَلاَ شُكُوراً
metadata.Tafsir: ((Saying)) that is inwardly, because they did not utter this openly but Allah informed us about the genuineness of their hearts: (We feed you, for the sake of Allah only) we feed you for the sake of Allah's reward and beneficence only. (We wish for no reward) with which to pay us back (nor thanks from you) nor gratitude from you;

translation: (Saying): "We feed you seeking Allâh’s Countenance only. We wish for no reward, nor thanks from you.

metadata.arabic: إِنَّا نَخَافُ مِن رَّبِّنَا يَوْماً عَبُوساً قَمْطَرِيراً
metadata.Tafsir: (Lo! we fear from our Lord) from the punishment of our Lord (a day of frowning) when faces are frowning (and of fate) a hard day whose torment and horrors are severe.

translation: "Verily, We fear from our Lord a Day, hard and distressful, that will make the faces look horrible (from extreme dislike to it)."

metadata.arabic: فَوَقَٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ شَرَّ ذَلِكَ ٱلْيَومِ وَلَقَّاهُمْ نَضْرَةً وَسُرُوراً
metadata.Tafsir: (Therefore Allah hath warded from them the evil of that day) the torment of that day, (and hath made them find) and has given them (brightness) bright and beautiful faces (and joy) in their hearts;

translation: So Allâh saved them from the evil of that Day, and gave them Nadrah (a light of beauty) and joy.

metadata.arabic: وَجَزَاهُمْ بِمَا صَبَرُواْ جَنَّةً وَحَرِيراً
metadata.Tafsir: (And hath awarded them for all that they endured) in the life of the world of poverty and misfortunes, (a Garden and silk attire;

translation: And their recompense shall be Paradise, and silken garments, because they were patient.

metadata.arabic: مُّتَّكِئِينَ فِيهَا عَلَىٰ ٱلأَرَائِكِ لاَ يَرَوْنَ فِيهَا شَمْساً وَلاَ زَمْهَرِيراً
metadata.Tafsir: (Reclining therein) sitting comfortably in the Garden (upon couches) in curtained canopies, (they will find there neither (heat of) a sun nor bitter cold) He says: they are touched neither by the heat of the sun nor by cold.

translation: Reclining therein on raised thrones, they will see there neither the excessive heat of the sun, nor the excessive bitter cold, (as in Paradise there is no sun and no moon).

metadata.arabic: وَدَانِيَةً عَلَيْهِمْ ظِلاَلُهَا وَذُلِّلَتْ قُطُوفُهَا تَذْلِيلاً
metadata.Tafsir: (The shade) of trees (thereof is close upon them and the clustered fruits thereof bow down) are made close and available to them.

translation: And the shade thereof is close upon them, and the bunches of fruit thereof will hang low within their reach.

metadata.arabic: وَيُطَافُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِآنِيَةٍ مِّن فِضَّةٍ وَأَكْوابٍ كَانَتْ قَوَارِيرَاْ
metadata.Tafsir: (Goblets of silver are brought round for them) by servants, (and beakers (as) of glass) without handles or covers

translation: And amongst them will be passed round vessels of silver and cups of crystal -

metadata.arabic: قَوَارِيرَاْ مِن فِضَّةٍ قَدَّرُوهَا تَقْدِيراً
metadata.Tafsir: ((Bright as) glass but (made) of silver, which they (themselves) have measured) in the hands of slave youths (to the measure (of their deeds)) it is also said that the drink is so measured that it is neither more nor less than what is required.

translation: Crystal-clear, made of silver. They will determine the measure thereof (according to their wishes).

metadata.arabic: وَيُسْقَوْنَ فِيهَا كَأْساً كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا زَنجَبِيلاً
metadata.Tafsir: (There) in the Garden (are they watered with a cup) of wine (whereof the mixture is of Zanjabil,

translation: And they will be given to drink there of a cup (of wine) mixed with Zanjabîl (ginger),

metadata.arabic: عَيْناً فِيهَا تُسَمَّىٰ سَلْسَبِيلاً
metadata.Tafsir: The water of a spring therein) in the Garden, (named Salsabil.

translation: A spring there, called Salsabîl.

metadata.arabic: وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدَانٌ مُّخَلَّدُونَ إِذَا رَأَيْتَهُمْ حَسِبْتَهُمْ لُؤْلُؤاً مَّنثُوراً
metadata.Tafsir: There wait on them youths of immortal youths) in Paradise who never die or are taken out of it; it is also said this means: youths wearing beautiful garments, (whom, when you see) O Muhammad, (thou wouldst take for scattered pearls) because of their brightness; and it is also said this means: because of their scatteredness.

translation: And round about them will (serve) boys of everlasting youth. If you see them, you would think them scattered pearls.

metadata.arabic: وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ ثَمَّ رَأَيْتَ نَعِيماً وَمُلْكاً كَبِيراً
metadata.Tafsir: (When thou seest) O Muhammad, (thou wilt see there) in the Garden (bliss) lasting bliss for its dwellers (and high estate) none enters in on them except with greetings of peace and permission.

translation: And when you look there (in Paradise), you will see a delight (that cannot be imagined), and a great dominion.

metadata.arabic: عَالِيَهُمْ ثِيَابُ سُندُسٍ خُضْرٌ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٌ وَحُلُّوۤاْ أَسَاوِرَ مِن فِضَّةٍ وَسَقَاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ شَرَاباً طَهُوراً
metadata.Tafsir: (Their raiment will be fine green silk and gold embroidery. Bracelets of silver will they wear. Their Lord will slake their thirst with a pure drink) pure from filth; it is also said this means: Allah purifies them from hatred, cheating and enmity.

translation: Their garments will be of fine green silk, and gold embroidery. They will be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them a pure drink.

metadata.arabic: إِنَّ هَـٰذَا كَانَ لَكُمْ جَزَآءً وَكَانَ سَعْيُكُم مَّشْكُوراً
metadata.Tafsir: (Lo! This) which I have described to you of food, drink and raiment (is a reward for you) is a reward from Allah. (Your endeavour (upon earth) hath found acceptance) your works were accepted and made to grow.

translation: (And it will be said to them): "Verily, this is a reward for you, and your endeavour has been accepted."

metadata.arabic: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ تَنزِيلاً
metadata.Tafsir: (Lo! We, even We, have revealed unto thee the Qur'an) We have sent you Gabriel with the Qur'an, (a revelation) in instalments: one, two and three verses at a time;

translation: Verily, it is We Who have sent down the Qur’ân to you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) by stages.

metadata.arabic: فَٱصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلاَ تُطِعْ مِنْهُمْ ءَاثِماً أَوْ كَفُوراً
metadata.Tafsir: (So submit patiently to thy Lord's command) to your Lord's decree; and it is also said this means: be patient in conveying the message of your Lord, (and obey not of them) of the disbelievers of Quraysh (any guilty one) any lewd and liar one, i.e. al-Walid Ibn al-Mughirah (or disbeliever) in Allah, i.e. 'Utbah Ibn Rabi'ah.

translation: Therefore be patient (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) with constancy to the Command of your Lord (Allâh, by doing your duty to Him and by conveying His Message to mankind), and obey neither a sinner nor a disbeliever among them.

metadata.arabic: وَٱذْكُرِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلاً
metadata.Tafsir: (Remember the name of thy Lord) pray by the command of your Lord (at morn and evening) i.e. the prayers of Fajr, Zuhr and 'Asr.

translation: And remember the Name of your Lord every morning and afternoon [i.e. offering of the Morning (Fajr), Zuhr, and ‘Asr prayers].

metadata.arabic: وَمِنَ ٱللَّيْلِ فَٱسْجُدْ لَهُ وَسَبِّحْهُ لَيْلاً طَوِيلاً
metadata.Tafsir: (And worship Him (a portion) of the night) pray the prayer of Maghrib and 'Isha'. (And glorify Him through the livelong night) pray to Him at night, this refers to supererogatory prayers; it is also said that the night prayer was made compulsory on him but not on his Companions.

translation: And during night, prostrate yourself to Him (i.e. the offering of Maghrib and ‘Ishâ’ prayers), and glorify Him a long night through (i.e. Tahajjud prayer).

metadata.arabic: إِنَّ هَـٰؤُلاَءِ يُحِبُّونَ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ وَيَذَرُونَ وَرَآءَهُمْ يَوْماً ثَقِيلاً
metadata.Tafsir: (Lo! These) the people of Mecca (love fleeting life) love striving for the life of the world, (and put behind them (the remembrance of)) and refrain from striving for the day which is ahead of them (a grievous day) whose torment and horrors are severe.

translation: Verily, these (disbelievers) love the present life of this world, and put behind them a heavy Day (that will be hard).

metadata.arabic: نَّحْنُ خَلَقْنَاهُمْ وَشَدَدْنَآ أَسْرَهُمْ وَإِذَا شِئْنَا بَدَّلْنَآ أَمْثَالَهُمْ تَبْدِيلاً
metadata.Tafsir: (We, even We, created them) i.e. the people of Mecca, (and strengthened their frame) and made their constitution strong. (And when We will, We can replace them, bringing others like them) i.e. We destroy them (in their stead) He says: if We had willed, We would have destroyed these sinful and disbelieving people and brought instead of them people who are better and more obedient.

translation: It is We Who created them, and We have made them of strong built. And when We will, We can replace them with others like them with a complete replacement.

metadata.arabic: إِنَّ هَـٰذِهِ تَذْكِرَةٌ فَمَن شَآءَ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ سَبِيلاً
metadata.Tafsir: (Lo! this is an Admonishment) from Allah, (that whosoever will may choose a way unto his Lord) that whoever will may believe in Allah's divine Oneness and return to his Lord.

translation: Verily, this (Verse of the Qur’ân) is an admonition, so whosoever wills, let him take a Path to his Lord (Allâh).

metadata.arabic: وَمَا تَشَآءُونَ إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيماً حَكِيماً
metadata.Tafsir: (Yet ye will not) good or evil, faith or disbelief, (unless Allah willeth) that you will it. (Lo! Allah is Knower) of what you will whether it is good or evil, (Wise) He decreed that you do not will anything of good or evil except that which He wills.

translation: But you cannot will, unless Allâh wills. Verily, Allâh is Ever All-Knowing, All-Wise.

metadata.arabic: يُدْخِلُ مَن يَشَآءُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ وَٱلظَّالِمِينَ أَعَدَّ لَهُمْ عَذَاباً أَلِيماً
metadata.Tafsir: (He maketh whom He will to enter His mercy) He honours whoever deserves it with the religion of Islam, (and for evil-doers) the disbelieving idolaters (hath prepared) soon in the Hereafter (a painful doom) whose pain extends to their hearts'.

translation: He will admit to His Mercy whom He wills and as for the Zâlimûn - (polytheists, wrong-doers) He has prepared a painful torment.

metadata.arabic: وَٱلْمُرْسَلاَتِ عُرْفاً
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said concerning the interpretation of Allah's saying (By the emissaries, (sent) one after another): '(By the emissaries, (sent) one after another) He says: Allah swears by the many angels who are sent one after another, just like horses follow one another; it is also said that these are the angels who are sent with the good, i.e. Gabriel, Michael and Seraphiel.

translation: By the winds (or angels or the Messengers of Allâh) sent forth one after another.

metadata.arabic: فَٱلْعَاصِفَاتِ عَصْفاً
metadata.Tafsir: (By the raging hurricanes) and He swore by the violent hurricanes which blow away people's houses,

translation: And by the winds that blow violently.

metadata.arabic: وٱلنَّاشِرَاتِ نَشْراً
metadata.Tafsir: (By those which cause earth's vegetation to revive) and He swore by the rain, i.e. He swore by the clouds from which comes the rain; it is also said: this refers to the angels who spread the Scripture;

translation: And by the winds that scatter clouds and rain.

metadata.arabic: فَٱلْفَارِقَاتِ فَرْقاً
metadata.Tafsir: (By those who winnow with a winnowing) and He swore by the angels who differentiate between the Truth and falsehood; it is also said that this refers to the verses of the Qur'an which distinguishes the Truth from falsehood, the lawful from the unlawful; and it is also said that these three refer to the angels,

translation: And by the Verses (of the Qur’ân) that separate the right from the wrong.

metadata.arabic: فَٱلْمُلْقِيَٰتِ ذِكْراً
metadata.Tafsir: (By those who bring down the Reminder) and He swore by those who bring down the revelations,

translation: And by the angels that bring the revelations to the Messengers,

metadata.arabic: عُذْراً أَوْ نُذْراً
metadata.Tafsir: (To excuse) to leave no excuse for one to think that Allah is an oppressor or transgressor (or to warn) His created beings from His chastisement; it is also said that (to excuse) refers to that which He has made lawful while (or to warn) refers to that which He has made unlawful; and it is also said (to excuse) refers to His commands while (or to warn) refers to His prohibitions; Allah swore by all these things,

translation: To cut off all excuses or to warn.

metadata.arabic: إِنَّمَا تُوعَدُونَ لَوَٰقِعٌ
metadata.Tafsir: (Surely that which ye are promised) of reward and punishment in the Hereafter (will befall) will happen and visit you.

translation: Surely, what you are promised must come to pass.

metadata.arabic: فَإِذَا ٱلنُّجُومُ طُمِسَتْ
metadata.Tafsir: Allah then showed when this will be, saying: (So when the stars are put out) when the light of the stars is gone,

translation: Then when the stars lose their lights.

metadata.arabic: وَإِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ فُرِجَتْ
metadata.Tafsir: (And when the sky is riven asunder,

translation: And when the heaven is cleft asunder.

metadata.arabic: وَإِذَا ٱلْجِبَالُ نُسِفَتْ
metadata.Tafsir: And when the mountains are blown away,

translation: And when the mountains are blown away.

metadata.arabic: وَإِذَا ٱلرُّسُلُ أُقِّتَتْ
metadata.Tafsir: And when the messengers are brought unto their time appointed) and when the messengers are gathered.

translation: And when the Messengers are gathered to their time appointed.

metadata.arabic: لأَيِّ يَوْمٍ أُجِّلَتْ
metadata.Tafsir: (For what day is the time appointed) for these things? He says: for what day has its Master delayed it.

translation: For what Day are these signs postponed?

metadata.arabic: لِيَوْمِ ٱلْفَصْلِ
metadata.Tafsir: Allah then explained, saying: (For the Day of Decision) when differences between people will be settled.

translation: For the Day of Sorting Out (the men of Paradise from the men destined for Hell).

metadata.arabic: وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا يَوْمُ ٱلْفَصْلِ
metadata.Tafsir: (And what will convey unto thee) O Muhammad (what the Day of Decision is!) How would you know about the Day of Decision?

translation: And what will explain to you what is the Day of Sorting Out?

metadata.arabic: وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Woe) a valley in Gehenna running with blood and puss; and it is also said: a well in the Fire; and it is also said that this refers to severe punishment (unto the repudiators) the disbelievers in Allah, the Scripture, the Messenger and resurrection after death (on that day) the Day of Judgement!

translation: Woe that Day to the deniers (of the Day of Resurrection)!

metadata.arabic: أَلَمْ نُهْلِكِ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Destroyed We not the former folk) by means of death as well as chastisement,

translation: Did We not destroy the ancients?

metadata.arabic: ثُمَّ نُتْبِعُهُمُ ٱلآخِرِينَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Then caused the latter folk to follow after) through death and chastisement?

translation: So shall We make later generations to follow them.

metadata.arabic: كَذَلِكَ نَفْعَلُ بِٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Thus deal We ever with the guilty) with the idolaters among your folk.

translation: Thus do We deal with the Mujrimûn (polytheists, disbelievers, sinners, criminals).

metadata.arabic: وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Woe) severe punishment (unto the repudiators) to the deniers of resurrection after death from among the people of your folk (on that day) the Day of Judgement!

translation: Woe that Day to the deniers (of the Day of Resurrection)!

metadata.arabic: أَلَمْ نَخْلُقكُّم مِّن مَّآءٍ مَّهِينٍ
metadata.Tafsir: (Did We not create you) O disbelievers (from a base fluid) from a flimsy sperm drop

translation: Did We not create you from a despised water (semen)?

metadata.arabic: فَجَعَلْنَاهُ فِي قَرَارٍ مَّكِينٍ
metadata.Tafsir: (Which We laid up in a safe abode) in the woman's womb.

translation: Then We placed it in a place of safety (womb),

metadata.arabic: إِلَىٰ قَدَرٍ مَّعْلُومٍ
metadata.Tafsir: (For a known term) until the time of its birth after nine months or less or more?

translation: For a known period (determined by gestation)?

metadata.arabic: فَقَدَرْنَا فَنِعْمَ ٱلْقَادِرُونَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Thus We arranged) its creation; it is also said this means: We controlled its creation; it is also said this means: and We fashioned its creation in the woman's womb. (How excellent is Our arranging!) how excellent is what We created and fashioned!

translation: So We did measure; and We are the Best to measure (the things).

metadata.arabic: وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Woe) severe punishment (unto the repudiators) of faith and resurrection after death (on that day) on the Day of Judgement!

translation: Woe that Day to the deniers (of the Day of Resurrection)!

metadata.arabic: أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ ٱلأَرْضَ كِفَاتاً
metadata.Tafsir: (Have We not made the earth a receptacle) to contain them

translation: Have We not made the earth a receptacle

metadata.arabic: أَحْيَآءً وَأَمْوٰتاً
metadata.Tafsir: (Both for the living) on its surface (and the dead) in its belly; it is also said this means: We made the earth a channel for both the living and the dead,

translation: For the living and the dead?

metadata.arabic: وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا رَوَاسِيَ شَامِخَاتٍ وَأَسْقَيْنَاكُم مَّآءً فُرَاتاً
metadata.Tafsir: (And placed therein) in the earth (high mountains) firm mountains well-steeped in their locations (and given you) O repudiators (to drink sweet water therein) and it is said fine water?

translation: And have placed therein firm, and tall mountains, and have given you to drink sweet water?

metadata.arabic: وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Woe) severe punishment (unto the repudiators) of faith and the resurrection (on that day) the Day of Judgement!

translation: Woe that Day to the deniers (of the Day of Resurrection)!

metadata.arabic: ٱنطَلِقُوۤاْ إِلَىٰ مَا كُنتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Depart) O repudiators (unto that (doom) which ye used to deny) in the life of the world, claiming that it will never take place;

translation: (It will be said to the disbelievers): "Depart you to that which you used to deny!

metadata.arabic: ٱنطَلِقُوۤاْ إِلَىٰ ظِلٍّ ذِي ثَلاَثِ شُعَبٍ
metadata.Tafsir: The angels who are the keepers of the Fire will say to them after the end of reckoning: (Depart) O deniers (unto the shadow) caused by the smoke of the Fire (falling threefold) three groups.

translation: "Depart you to a shadow (of Hell-Fire smoke ascending) in three columns,

metadata.arabic: لاَّ ظَلِيلٍ وَلاَ يُغْنِي مِنَ ٱللَّهَبِ
metadata.Tafsir: ((Which yet is) no relief) from the heat of the Fire (nor shelter from the flame) of the Fire.

translation: Neither shady, nor of any use against the fierce flame of the Fire."

metadata.arabic: إِنَّهَا تَرْمِي بِشَرَرٍ كَٱلْقَصْرِ
metadata.Tafsir: (Lo! It) i.e. the Fire (throweth up sparks like the castles) like the bases of huge trees,

translation: Verily, it (Hell) throws sparks (huge) as Al-Qasr (a fort or a huge log of wood),

metadata.arabic: كَأَنَّهُ جِمَٰلَتٌ صُفْرٌ
metadata.Tafsir: ((Or) as it might be camels of bright yellow hue) black camels.

translation: As if they were yellow camels or bundles of ropes.

metadata.arabic: وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Woe) severe punishment (unto the repudiators) of faith and the resurrection (on that day) the Day of Judgement!

translation: Woe that Day to the deniers (of the Day of Resurrection)!

metadata.arabic: هَـٰذَا يَوْمُ لاَ يَنطِقُونَ
metadata.Tafsir: (This is a day wherein they speak not) in some places and speak in others,

translation: That will be a Day when they shall not speak (during some part of it),

metadata.arabic: وَلاَ يُؤْذَنُ لَهُمْ فَيَعْتَذِرُونَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Nor are they suffered) nor are they given permission (to put forth excuses.

translation: And they will not be permitted to put forth any excuse.

metadata.arabic: وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
metadata.Tafsir: Woe) severe punishment (unto the repudiators) of faith and the resurrection (on that day) the Day of Judgement!

translation: Woe that Day to the deniers (of the Day of Resurrection)!

metadata.arabic: هَـٰذَا يَوْمُ ٱلْفَصْلِ جَمَعْنَٰكُمْ وَٱلأَوَّلِينَ
metadata.Tafsir: (This is the Day of Decision) regarding created beings, (We have brought you) O disbelievers (and the men of old together) as well as those who were after you.

translation: That will be a Day of Decision! We have brought you and the men of old together!

metadata.arabic: فَإِن كَانَ لَكمُ كَيْدٌ فَكِيدُونِ
metadata.Tafsir: (If now ye have any wit) if you have the power to do anything to Me, (outwit Me) then do it; it is also said that this means: if you have any scheme against Me, then execute it.

translation: So if you have a plot, use it against Me (Allâh جل جلاله)!

metadata.arabic: وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Woe) severe punishment (unto the repudiators) of faith and the resurrection (on that day) the Day of Judgement!

translation: Woe that Day to the deniers (of the Day of Resurrection)!

metadata.arabic: إِنَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ فِي ظِلاَلٍ وَعُيُونٍ
metadata.Tafsir: Allah then explained the abode of the believers, saying: (Lo! those who kept their duty) those who ward off disbelief, idolatry and indecencies (are amid shade) amid the shade of trees (and fountains) plain, running water,

translation: Verily, the Muttaqûn (the pious. See V.2:2) shall be amidst shades and springs.

metadata.arabic: وَفَوَاكِهَ مِمَّا يَشْتَهُونَ
metadata.Tafsir: (And fruits) different kinds of fruit (such as they desire).

translation: And fruits, such as they desire.

metadata.arabic: كُلُواْ وَٱشْرَبُواْ هَنِيـۤئاً بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
metadata.Tafsir: Allah will say to them (Eat) of the fruits, (drink) from the rivers (and welcome) fearing no sickness or death, (O ye blessed, in return for what ye did) and said of good in the life of the world.

translation: "Eat and drink comfortably for that which you used to do."

metadata.arabic: إِنَّا كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Thus do We reward the good) in words and deeds.

translation: Verily, thus We reward the Muhsinûn (good-doers. See V.2:112).

metadata.arabic: وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Woe) severe punishment (unto the repudiators) of faith and the resurrection (on that day) the Day of Judgement!

translation: Woe that Day to the deniers (of the Day of Resurrection)!

metadata.arabic: كُلُواْ وَتَمَتَّعُواْ قَلِيلاً إِنَّكُمْ مُّجْرِمُونَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Eat) O disbelievers (and take your ease a little) in the life of the world. (Lo! ye are guilty) you are idolaters and your destination in the Hereafter will be the Fire. This is a threat to them from Allah.

translation: (O you disbelievers)! Eat and enjoy yourselves (in this worldly life) for a little while. Verily, you are the Mujrimûn (polytheists, disbelievers, sinners, criminals).

metadata.arabic: وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Woe) severe punishment (unto the repudiators) of faith and the resurrection (on that day) the Day of Judgement!

translation: Woe that Day to the deniers (of the Day of Resurrection)!

metadata.arabic: وَإذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱرْكَعُواْ لاَ يَرْكَعُونَ
metadata.Tafsir: (When it is said unto them) to the disbelievers when they were in the life of the world: (Bow down) submit to Allah by believing in His divine Oneness, (they bow not down!) they did not submit to Allah by accepting His divine Oneness; it is also said that they will be asked to do so in the Hereafter, when Allah will say to them: " bow down, if you are truthful that you believed in that which you now claim " , this is because they said: " By Allah, our Lord, we were not idolaters ". But they will not be able to bow down and their bodies will remain erect and stiff. It is also said that this verse was revealed about Thaqif who said: " we will not bend down to bow or prostrate ".

translation: And when it is said to them: "Bow down yourself (in prayer)!" They bow not down (offer not their prayers).

metadata.arabic: وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Woe) severe punishment (unto the repudiators) to the disbelievers in Allah, His Messenger, Scripture and the resurrection (on that day) the day of Judgement!

translation: Woe that Day to the deniers (of the Day of Resurrection)!

metadata.arabic: فَبِأَيِّ حَدِيثٍ بَعْدَهُ يُؤْمِنُونَ
metadata.Tafsir: (In what statement) in what Scripture, (after this) after the Book of Allah, (will they believe) if they do not believe in these tidings?'

translation: Then in what statement after this (the Qur’ân) will they believe?

metadata.arabic: عَمَّ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (Whereof do they question one another?): He says: 'what are they-meaning the people of Quraysh-talking about?'

translation: What are they asking (one another) about?

metadata.arabic: عَنِ ٱلنَّبَإِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
metadata.Tafsir: ((It is) of the awful tidings) they are talking about the tidings of the noble, glorious and great Qur'an,

translation: About the great news, (i.e. Islâmic Monotheism, the Qur’ân, which Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم brought and the Day of Resurrection)

metadata.arabic: ٱلَّذِي هُمْ فِيهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Concerning which they are in disagreement) some of them disbelieve in Muhammad (pbuh) and in the Qur'an while others believe in them. This is because whenever Gabriel brought down a section of the Qur'an to the Prophet (pbuh) and he recited it to them, they used to talk about it, and some of them would believe while others would persist in their disbelief.

translation: About which they are in disagreement.

metadata.arabic: كَلاَّ سَيَعْلَمُونَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Nay) this is a reply to the disbelievers, (but they will come to know!) They will come to know upon the advent of death what will be done with them.

translation: Nay, they will come to know!

metadata.arabic: ثُمَّ كَلاَّ سَيَعْلَمُونَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Nay) truly, (again, but they will come to know!) They will come to know in the grave what will be done with them. This is a threat from Allah to those who disbelieved in Muhammad (pbuh) and in the Qur'an.

translation: Nay, again, they will come to know!

metadata.arabic: أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ ٱلأَرْضَ مِهَٰداً
metadata.Tafsir: Allah then mentioned the blessings He bestowed upon them, saying: (Have We not made the earth an expanse) and a place to sleep,

translation: Have We not made the earth as a bed,

metadata.arabic: وَٱلْجِبَالَ أَوْتَاداً
metadata.Tafsir: (And the high hills bulwarks) for it so that it does not sway?

translation: And the mountains as pegs?

metadata.arabic: وَخَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَزْوَاجاً
metadata.Tafsir: (And We have created you in pairs) male and female,

translation: And We have created you in pairs (male and female, tall and short, good and bad, etc.).

metadata.arabic: وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتاً
metadata.Tafsir: (And have appointed your sleep for repose) a repose for your bodies; and it is said this means: nice and beautiful,

translation: And We have made your sleep as a thing for rest.

metadata.arabic: وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلَّيلَ لِبَاساً
metadata.Tafsir: (And have appointed the night as a cloak) and it is said this means: a dwelling,

translation: And We have made the night as a covering (through its darkness),

metadata.arabic: وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلنَّهَارَ مَعَاشاً
metadata.Tafsir: (And have appointed the day for livelihood) for seeking livelihood.

translation: And We have made the day for livelihood.

metadata.arabic: وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعاً شِدَاداً
metadata.Tafsir: (And We have built) and We have created (above you) above your heads (seven strong (heavens)) seven thick heavens,

translation: And We have built above you seven strong (heavens),

metadata.arabic: وَجَعَلْنَا سِرَاجاً وَهَّاجاً
metadata.Tafsir: (And have appointed a dazzling lamp) and have appointed a radiant sun for the children of Adam,

translation: And We have made (therein) a shining lamp (sun).

metadata.arabic: وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمُعْصِرَاتِ مَآءً ثَجَّاجاً
metadata.Tafsir: (And have sent down from the rainy clouds abundant Water,

translation: And We have sent down from the rainy clouds abundant water.

metadata.arabic: لِّنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبّاً وَنَبَاتاً
metadata.Tafsir: Thereby to produce grain and plant) to produce through the rain all kinds of grains and plants,

translation: That We may produce therewith corn and vegetations,

metadata.arabic: وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفَافاً
metadata.Tafsir: (And gardens of thick foliage) and it is also said this means: different kinds of foliage.

translation: And gardens of thick growth.

metadata.arabic: إِنَّ يَوْمَ ٱلْفَصْلِ كَانَ مِيقَاتاً
metadata.Tafsir: (Lo! the Day of Decision is a fixed time) it is the appointed time when the people of old and later generations will be gathered,

translation: Verily, the Day of Decision is a fixed time,

metadata.arabic: يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِي ٱلصُّورِ فَتَأْتُونَ أَفْوَاجاً
metadata.Tafsir: (A day when the trumpet is blown) the blowing of the resurrection, (and ye come in multitudes) host after host and group after group,

translation: The Day when the Trumpet will be blown, and you shall come forth in crowds (groups after groups). [Tafsir At-Tabari]

metadata.arabic: وَفُتِحَتِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ فَكَانَتْ أَبْوَاباً
metadata.Tafsir: (And the heaven is opened) and the gates of heaven are opened (and becometh as gates) and becomes different roads,

translation: And the heaven shall be opened, and it will become as gates,

metadata.arabic: وَسُيِّرَتِ ٱلْجِبَالُ فَكَانَتْ سَرَاباً
metadata.Tafsir: (And the hills are set in motion) on the face of the earth (and become as a mirage.

translation: And the mountains shall be moved away from their places and they will be as if they were a mirage.

metadata.arabic: إِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ كَانَتْ مِرْصَاداً
metadata.Tafsir: Lo! Hell lurketh in ambush) the Fire is a detention and prison,

translation: Truly, Hell is a place of ambush -

metadata.arabic: لِّلطَّاغِينَ مَآباً
metadata.Tafsir: (A home for the rebellious) a point of return for the disbelievers.

translation: A dwelling place for the Tâghûn (those who transgress the boundary limits set by Allâh like polytheists, disbelievers in the Oneness of Allâh, hyprocrites, sinners, criminals),

metadata.arabic: لاَّبِثِينَ فِيهَآ أَحْقَاباً
metadata.Tafsir: (They will abide therein for ages) they will abide in the Fire for ages and ages, each age consisting of 80 years, each year being 360 days and each day is the equivalent of 1,000 years of the years of the life of the world; it is also said that none knows the exact duration of these ages save Allah, and therefore these ages are never interrupted.

translation: They will abide therein for ages.

metadata.arabic: لاَّ يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا بَرْداً وَلاَ شَرَاباً
metadata.Tafsir: (Therein) in the Fire (taste they neither coolness) cool water; and it is also said this means: sleep (nor (any) drink) cold drink

translation: Nothing cool shall they taste therein, nor any drink.

metadata.arabic: إِلاَّ حَمِيماً وَغَسَّاقاً
metadata.Tafsir: (Save boiling water and a paralysing cold) and it is also said this means: filthy water:

translation: Except boiling water, and dirty wound discharges -

metadata.arabic: جَزَآءً وِفَاقاً
metadata.Tafsir: (Reward proportioned (to their evil deeds)) a reward which is commensurate with their works.

translation: An exact recompense (according to their evil crimes).

metadata.arabic: إِنَّهُمْ كَانُواْ لاَ يَرْجُونَ حِسَاباً
metadata.Tafsir: (For lo! they looked not) while in the life of the world (for a reckoning) they did not fear the chastisement of the Hereafter nor did they believe in it;

translation: For verily, they used not to look for a reckoning.

metadata.arabic: وَكَذَّبُواْ بِآيَاتِنَا كِذَّاباً
metadata.Tafsir: (They called Our revelations) Our Scripture and Messenger (false with strong denial.

translation: But they belied Our Ayât (proofs, evidence, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, and that which Our Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم brought) completely.

metadata.arabic: وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَاهُ كِتَاباً
metadata.Tafsir: Everything) regarding the works of the children of Adam (have We recorded in a Book) We wrote it down in the Guarded or Preserved Tablet.

translation: And all things We have recorded in a Book.

metadata.arabic: فَذُوقُواْ فَلَن نَّزِيدَكُمْ إِلاَّ عَذَاباً
metadata.Tafsir: (So taste) the chastisement in the Fire. (No increase do We give you) in the Fire (save of torment) one kind of torment after another.

translation: So taste you (the results of your evil actions). No increase shall We give you, except in torment.

metadata.arabic: إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ مَفَازاً
metadata.Tafsir: (Lo! for the duteous) for those who ward off disbelief, idolatry and indecencies (is achievement) safety from the Fire and nearness of Allah

translation: Verily, for the Muttaqûn, there will be a success (Paradise);

metadata.arabic: حَدَآئِقَ وَأَعْنَاباً
metadata.Tafsir: (Gardens) of trees and palm-trees (enclosed and vineyards,

translation: Gardens and vineyards,

metadata.arabic: وَكَوَاعِبَ أَتْرَاباً
metadata.Tafsir: And maidens for companions) who are all of the same age: 33 years of age,

translation: And young full-breasted (mature) maidens of equal age,

metadata.arabic: وَكَأْساً دِهَاقاً
metadata.Tafsir: (And a full cup) one cup after another.

translation: And a full cup (of wine).

metadata.arabic: لاَّ يَسْمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغْواً وَلاَ كِذَّاباً
metadata.Tafsir: (There) in Paradise (hear they) the inhabitants of the Garden (never vain discourse) oaths or falsehood, (nor lying) they do not lie to each other.

translation: No Laghw (dirty, false, evil talk) shall they hear therein, nor lying;

metadata.arabic: جَزَآءً مِّن رَّبِّكَ عَطَآءً حِسَاباً
metadata.Tafsir: (Requital) a reward (from thy Lord a gift) that He bestows upon them in the Garden (in payment) ten rewards for each good deed; and it is also said this means: reward in proportion to their good deeds

translation: A reward from your Lord, an ample calculated gift (according to the best of their good deeds),

metadata.arabic: رَّبِّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ لاَ يَمْلِكُونَ مِنْهُ خِطَاباً
metadata.Tafsir: (Lord of the heavens and the earth, and (all) that is between them) of creation and marvels, (the Beneficent) He is the Beneficent; (with Whom none) none of His slaves, i.e. the angels as well as others (can converse) with regard to intercession until Allah gives them permission to do so.

translation: (From) the Lord of the heavens and the earth, and whatsoever is in between them, the Most Gracious, with Whom they cannot dare to speak (on the Day of Resurrection except by His Leave).

metadata.arabic: يَوْمَ يَقُومُ ٱلرُّوحُ وَٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ صَفّاً لاَّ يَتَكَلَّمُونَ إِلاَّ مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ وَقَالَ صَوَاباً
metadata.Tafsir: (On the day when the angels and the Spirit) Gabriel; and it is also said: this is a created being whose tremendousness only Allah knows; Ibn Mas'ud also said: the Spirit is an angel greater than every thing save the Throne, and this angel glorifies Allah each day 12,000 formulas of glorification, and which each glorification he utters Allah creates an angel who seeks forgiveness for the believers until the Day of Judgement; it is also said this refers to a group of angels who have feet and hands like those of humans (stand arrayed, they speak not) to intercede, (saving him whom the Beneficent alloweth) to intercede (and who speaketh right) truly “there is no deity save Allah”.

translation: The Day that Ar-Rûh [Jibrîl (Gabriel) or another angel] and the angels will stand forth in rows, they will not speak except him whom the Most Gracious (Allâh) allows, and he will speak what is right.

metadata.arabic: ذَلِكَ ٱلْيَوْمُ ٱلْحَقُّ فَمَن شَآءَ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ مَآباً
metadata.Tafsir: (That is the True Day) in which will happen what I have mentioned. (So whoso will should seek recourse) whoever will believe in Allah's divine Oneness and seek through his belief in Allah's divine Oneness a way of return (unto his Lord.

translation: That is (without doubt) the True Day. So, whosoever wills, let him seek a place with (or a way to) His Lord (by obeying Him in this worldly life)!

metadata.arabic: إِنَّآ أَنذَرْنَاكُمْ عَذَاباً قَرِيباً يَوْمَ يَنظُرُ ٱلْمَرْءُ مَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاهُ وَيَقُولُ ٱلْكَافِرُ يٰلَيْتَنِي كُنتُ تُرَاباً
metadata.Tafsir: Lo! We warn you) O people of Mecca (of a doom at hand) which will surely happen, (a day whereon a man will look) when the believer will look; and it is also said: when the disbeliever will look (on that which his own hands have sent before) have earned of good or evil, (and the disbeliever will cry: “Would that I were dust!”) with the beasts. Because of the horrors, severity and torment of that day, the disbeliever will wish to be turned into dust along with beasts. This will occur on the day when the first trumpet resounds'.

translation: Verily, We have warned you of a near torment - the Day when man will see that (the deeds) which his hands have sent forth, and the disbeliever will say: "Woe to me! Would that I were dust!"

metadata.arabic: وَٱلنَّازِعَاتِ غَرْقاً
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said concerning the interpretation of Allah's saying (By those who drag forth): '(By those who drag forth) He says: Allah swears by the angels who take away the souls of the disbelievers (to destruction) the souls of the disbelievers,

translation: By those (angels) who pull out (the souls of the disbelievers and the wicked) with great violence.

metadata.arabic: وَٱلنَّاشِطَاتِ نَشْطاً
metadata.Tafsir: (By the meteors rushing) and it is also said that He is here swearing by the angels who busy the disbelievers with grief and anxiety; it is also said that this refers to the souls of the believers which hasten to come out of their bodies in order to go to the Garden.

translation: By those (angels) who gently take out (the souls of the believers).

metadata.arabic: وَٱلسَّابِحَاتِ سَبْحاً
metadata.Tafsir: (By the lone stars floating) and it is also said that He is here swearing by the angels who take away the souls of the righteous slowly and gently and then let them rest; it is also said this refers to the souls of the believers,

translation: And by those that swim along (i.e. angels or planets in their orbits).

metadata.arabic: فَٱلسَّابِقَاتِ سَبْقاً
metadata.Tafsir: (By the angels hastening) and He swears by the angels who hasten to Paradise with the souls of the believers and to the Fire with the souls of the disbelievers; it is also said this refers to the souls of the believers that hasten to Paradise,

translation: And by those that press forward as in a race (i.e. the angels or stars or the horses).

metadata.arabic: فَٱلْمُدَبِّرَاتِ أَمْراً
metadata.Tafsir: (And those who govern the event) and He swears by the angels who govern the matters of the slaves, meaning Gabriel, Michael, Seraphiel and the angel of death. It is said that (those who govern the event) refers to the spears of soldiers, (the meteors rushing) refers to the ropes of soldiers and (the lone stars floating) refers to the ships of soldiers who fight at sea, (the ones who do the hastening) refers to the horses of soldiers, while (those who govern the event) refers to the generals of soldiers; it is also said that (the lone stars floating) refer to the sun, the moon, the day and the night. Allah swore by all these that the two blowings of the trumpet will take place, with an interval of 40 years separating the two blowings.

translation: And by those angels who arrange to do the Commands of their Lord, (so verily, you disbelievers will be called to account).

metadata.arabic: يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ ٱلرَّاجِفَةُ
metadata.Tafsir: So Allah said: (On the day when the first trump resoundeth) this refers to the first blowing of the trumpet when everything will quake.

translation: On the Day (when the first blowing of the Trumpet is blown), the earth and the mountains will shake violently (and everybody will die).

metadata.arabic: تَتْبَعُهَا ٱلرَّادِفَةُ
metadata.Tafsir: (And the second followeth it) this is the final blowing on the trumpet,

translation: The second blowing of the Trumpet follows it (and everybody will be resurrected).

metadata.arabic: قُلُوبٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَاجِفَةٌ
metadata.Tafsir: (On that day) which is the Day of Judgement (hearts beat painfully) the hearts are fearful

translation: (Some) hearts that Day will shake with fear and anxiety.

metadata.arabic: أَبْصَارُهَا خَاشِعَةٌ
metadata.Tafsir: (While eyes are downcast) abased

translation: Their eyes will be downcast.

metadata.arabic: يَقُولُونَ أَإِنَّا لَمَرْدُودُونَ فِي ٱلْحَافِرَةِ
metadata.Tafsir: ((Now) they) the disbelievers of Mecca: al-Nadr Ibn al-Harith and his host (are saying: Shall we really be restored to our first state) to the life of the world; and it is also said: from the graves

translation: They say: "Shall we indeed be returned to (our) former state of life?

metadata.arabic: أَإِذَا كُنَّا عِظَاماً نَّخِرَةً
metadata.Tafsir: (Even after we are crumbled bones?) Will Allah resurrect us? How is this possible?

translation: "Even after we are crumbled bones?"

metadata.arabic: قَالُواْ تِلْكَ إِذاً كَرَّةٌ خَاسِرَةٌ
metadata.Tafsir: The Prophet (pbuh) said to them: “Indeed, Allah will raise you again from the dead”. (They say: Then that would be a vain proceeding) that would be a failed attempt, because it will never happen.

translation: They say: "It would in that case, be a return with loss!"

metadata.arabic: فَإِنَّمَا هِيَ زَجْرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ
metadata.Tafsir: And so Allah said: (Surely it will need but one shout) one blow which does not require a second one, and this is the blow of the resurrection,

translation: But it will be only a single Zajrah [shout (i.e., the second blowing of the Trumpet)], (See Verse 37:19).

metadata.arabic: فَإِذَا هُم بِٱلسَّاهِرَةِ
metadata.Tafsir: (And lo! they will be awakened) on the face of the earth; and it is also said: in the land of the gathering.

translation: When behold, they find themselves on the surface of the earth alive after their death,

metadata.arabic: هَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ مُوسَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Hath there come unto thee) O Muhammad (the history of Moses) the story of Moses? Meaning: the story of Moses has already come to you; and it is also said this means: the story of Moses has not yet come to you.

translation: Has there come to you the story of Mûsâ (Moses)?

metadata.arabic: إِذْ نَادَاهُ رَبُّهُ بِٱلْوَادِ ٱلْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى
metadata.Tafsir: (How his Lord called him in the holy vale of Tuwa) the name of the valley; it was called so because it was traversed by so many prophets; it is also said: tread (Ta'), O Moses, with your feet on this valley because of its goodness and grace.

translation: When his Lord called him in the sacred valley of Tûwâ,

metadata.arabic: ٱذْهَبْ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: ((Saying:) Go thou) O Moses (unto Pharaoh. Lo! he hath rebelled) he is arrogant and too proud and has refused to believe in Allah

translation: Go to Fir‘aun (Pharaoh); verily he has transgressed all bounds (in crimes, sins, polytheism, disbelief).

metadata.arabic: فَقُلْ هَل لَّكَ إِلَىٰ أَن تَزَكَّىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (And say (unto him): Hast thou) O Pharaoh ((will) to grow (in grace)) will become righteous, surrender and believe in Allah's divine Oneness?

translation: And say to him: "Would you purify yourself (from the sin of disbelief by becoming a believer)?"

metadata.arabic: وَأَهْدِيَكَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَتَخْشَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Then I will guide thee) I will call you (to thy Lord and thou shalt fear (Him)) and therefore surrender to Him.

translation: "And that I guide you to your Lord, so you should fear Him?"

metadata.arabic: فَأَرَاهُ ٱلآيَةَ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (And he) Moses (showed him the tremendous token) the hand and the staff.

translation: Then [Mûsâ (Moses)] showed him the great sign (miracles).

metadata.arabic: فَكَذَّبَ وَعَصَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (But be denied) and said: this is not from Allah (and disobeyed) he refused the message,

translation: But [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] belied and disobeyed.

metadata.arabic: ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ يَسْعَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Then turned he away) from faith; and it is also said: from Moses (in haste) to his folk; and it is also said: to think what to do about Moses,

translation: Then he turned his back, striving (against Allâh).

metadata.arabic: فَحَشَرَ فَنَادَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Then gathered he) his army (and summoned) and delivered a sermon

translation: Then he gathered (his people) and cried aloud,

metadata.arabic: فَقَالَ أَنَاْ رَبُّكُمُ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (And proclaimed: “I (Pharaoh) am your Lord the Highest”.) I am your Highest Lord and the Lord of your idols, therefore, do not leave the worship of these idols.

translation: Saying: "I am your lord, most high."

metadata.arabic: فَأَخَذَهُ ٱللَّهُ نَكَالَ ٱلآخِرَةِ وَٱلأُوْلَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (So Allah seized him) Allah punished him ((and made him) an example for the after (life) and for the former) the punishment that he suffered in the life of the world is drowning and the punishment of the Hereafter will be in the Fire; it is also said that this means: Allah has punished him because of his former and latter pronouncements. His first pronouncement being: “I do not know of any other god for you except Me” and the second being (I am your Lord the Highest) and it is said that there is an interval of 40 years between the first and second pronouncements.

translation: So Allâh, seized him with punishment for his last and first transgression. [Tafsir At-Tabari]

metadata.arabic: إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِّمَن يَخْشَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Lo! Herein) in that which We did to Pharaoh and his host (is indeed a lesson) an admonition (for him who feareth) that which has been done to them.

translation: Verily, in this is an instructive admonition for whosoever fears Allâh.

metadata.arabic: ءَأَنتُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقاً أَمِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ بَنَاهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (Are ye) O people of Mecca (the harder to create) harder to resurrect and more perfect in your creation, (or is the heaven that He built?

translation: Are you more difficult to create or is the heaven that He constructed?

metadata.arabic: رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا فَسَوَّاهَا
metadata.Tafsir: He raised the height) its ceiling (thereof and ordered it) above the earth;

translation: He raised its height, and has perfected it.

metadata.arabic: وَأَغْطَشَ لَيْلَهَا وَأَخْرَجَ ضُحَاهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (And He made dark the night thereof, and He brought forth the morn thereof) and He made its day and sun clear.

translation: Its night He covers with darkness and its forenoon He brings out (with light)

metadata.arabic: وَٱلأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ دَحَاهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (And after that He spread the earth) even then He spread it on the water; it is also said: 2,000 years after that He spread it on the water,

translation: And after that He spread the earth,

metadata.arabic: أَخْرَجَ مِنْهَا مَآءَهَا وَمَرْعَاهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (And produced therefrom) from the earth (the water thereof) running water as well as the water buried deep in the belly of the earth (and the pasture thereof,

translation: And brought forth therefrom its water and its pasture.

metadata.arabic: وَٱلْجِبَالَ أَرْسَاهَا
metadata.Tafsir: And He made fast the hills) and He made the mountains firm,

translation: And the mountains He has fixed firmly,

metadata.arabic: مَتَاعاً لَّكُمْ وَلأَنْعَامِكُمْ
metadata.Tafsir: (A provision for you) water of benefit to you (and for your cattle) water and pasture benefit your cattle.

translation: (To be) a provision and benefit for you and your cattle.

metadata.arabic: فَإِذَا جَآءَتِ ٱلطَّآمَّةُ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (But when the great disaster cometh) but when the Hour comes, it will tower above everything and nothing will escape it,

translation: But when there comes the greatest catastrophe (i.e. the Day of Recompense) -

metadata.arabic: يَوْمَ يَتَذَكَّرُ ٱلإِنسَانُ مَا سَعَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (The day when man will call to mind) when the disbeliever, al-Nadr Ibn al-Harith and his host, will remember and know (his (whole) endeavour) the works he did in his state of disbelief,

translation: The Day when man shall remember what he strove for.

metadata.arabic: وَبُرِّزَتِ ٱلْجَحِيمُ لِمَن يَرَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (And hell will stand forth visible to him who seeth) to him who is ordained to enter it,

translation: And Hell-fire shall be made apparent in full view for (every) one who sees.

metadata.arabic: فَأَمَّا مَن طَغَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Then, as for him who rebelled) him who was too arrogant and proud and disbelieved in Allah, i.e. al-Nadr Ibn al-Harith Ibn 'Alqamah

translation: Then for him who transgressed all bounds, (in disbelief, oppression and evil deeds of disobedience to Allâh).

metadata.arabic: وَآثَرَ ٱلْحَيَاةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا
metadata.Tafsir: (And chose the life of the world) rather than the Hereafter and also chose disbelief rather than faith,

translation: And preferred the life of this world (by following his evil desires and lusts),

metadata.arabic: فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ هِيَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Lo! Hell will be his home) the Fire is the home of him who is thus.

translation: Verily, his abode will be Hell-fire;

metadata.arabic: وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ وَنَهَى ٱلنَّفْسَ عَنِ ٱلْهَوَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (But as for him who feared) upon committing a sin (to stand before his Lord) his standing before his Lord and abstains from engaging in sin (and restrained his soul from lust) from that which is unlawful, even though he desires it, this refers to Mus'ab Ibn 'Umayr.

translation: But as for him who feared standing before his Lord, and restrained himself from impure evil desires and lusts.

metadata.arabic: فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَنَّةَ هِيَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Lo! the Garden will be his home) Paradise will be the home of him who is thus.

translation: Verily, Paradise will be his abode.

metadata.arabic: يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلسَّاعَةِ أَيَّانَ مُرْسَٰهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (They ask thee) the disbelievers of Mecca ask you, O Muhammad, (of the Hour) about the advent of the Hour: (when will it come to port?) When is it going to happen? Because they disbelieved in it.

translation: They ask you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) about the Hour - when will be its appointed time?

metadata.arabic: فِيمَ أَنتَ مِن ذِكْرَٰهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (Why (ask they)? What hast thou to tell thereof?) What has it to do with you that you should mention it to them?

translation: You have no knowledge to say anything about it.

metadata.arabic: إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ مُنتَهَٰهَآ
metadata.Tafsir: (Unto thy Lord belongeth (knowledge of) the term thereof) the knowledge of its timing belongs to Allah.

translation: To your Lord belongs (the knowledge of) the term thereof?

metadata.arabic: إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُنذِرُ مَن يَخْشَٰهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (Thou art but a warner) you are but a warning messenger by means of the Qur'an (unto him who feareth it) to him who fears its advent.

translation: You (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) are only a warner for those who fear it,

metadata.arabic: كَأَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَهَا لَمْ يَلْبَثُوۤاْ إِلاَّ عَشِيَّةً أَوْ ضُحَٰهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (On the day when they behold it) i.e. the Hour, (it will be as if they had but tarried) in the graves (for an evening) the duration of an evening (or the morn thereof) or the duration of one morning'.

translation: The Day they see it, (it will be) as if they had not tarried (in this world) except an afternoon or a morning.

metadata.arabic: عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (He frowned): '(He frowned) He says: Muhammad (pbuh) showed a stern face (and turned away) his face

translation: (The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم) frowned and turned away.

metadata.arabic: أَن جَآءَهُ ٱلأَعْمَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Because the blind man came unto him) when 'Abdullah Ibn Umm Maktum came to him. His real name is 'Abdullah Ibn Shurayh. Umm Maktum was his father's mother. What happened is that the Prophet (pbuh) was sitting with a group of men among the nobles of Quraysh, among whom were his uncle al-'Abbas Ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, Umayyah Ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi and Safwan Ibn Umayyah, who were at that time disbelievers. The Prophet (pbuh) was admonishing and inviting them to Islam when Ibn Maktum came to him and said: “O Messenger of Allah! Teach me of that which Allah has taught you”. The Prophet (pbuh) turned his face from him because he was busy with these people. When this happened Allah revealed: he frowned and turned away because the blind man came unto him.

translation: Because there came to him the blind man (i.e. ‘Abdullâh bin Umm-Maktûm, who came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم while he was preaching to one or some of the Quraish chiefs).

metadata.arabic: وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّهُ يَزَّكَّىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (What could inform thee) O Muhammad (but that he might) i.e. the blind man (grow (in grace)) became righteous through the admonitions of the Qur'an

translation: And how can you know that he might become pure (from sins)?

metadata.arabic: أَوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنفَعَهُ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ
