metadata.Tafsir: (None bindeth as He then will bind) this can also be understood to mean: none punishes like this and none will inflict that kind of punishment except Allah.

translation: And none will bind (the wicked, disbelievers and polytheists) as He will bind.

metadata.arabic: يٰأَيَّتُهَا ٱلنَّفْسُ ٱلْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ
metadata.Tafsir: (But ah! thou soul at peace) which is safe from Allah's chastisement, true in its profession of Allah's divine Oneness, grateful for the blessings Allah bestowed upon it, patient with the trials of Allah, pleased with things decreed by Allah, and content with that which Allah gives!

translation: (It will be said to the pious believers of Islamic Monotheism): "O (you) the one in (complete) rest and satisfaction!

metadata.arabic: ٱرْجِعِي إِلَىٰ رَبِّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَّرْضِيَّةً
metadata.Tafsir: (Return unto thy Lord) return to that which Allah has prepared for you in the Garden; and it is also said this means: return to your master: the body, (content) with Allah's reward (in His good pleasure) because of its belief in Allah's divine Oneness!

translation: "Come back to your Lord well-pleased (yourself) and well-pleasing (unto Him)!

metadata.arabic: فَٱدْخُلِي فِي عِبَادِي
metadata.Tafsir: (Enter thou among My bondmen) enter you among My friends!

translation: "Enter you then among My (honoured) slaves,

metadata.arabic: وَٱدْخُلِي جَنَّتِي
metadata.Tafsir: (Enter thou My Garden) which I have prepared for you!'

translation: "And enter you My Paradise!"

metadata.arabic: لاَ أُقْسِمُ بِهَـٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدِ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (Nay, I swear by this city): '(Nay, I swear by this city) He says: I swear by the city of Mecca

translation: I swear by this city (Makkah);

metadata.arabic: وَأَنتَ حِلٌّ بِهَـٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدِ
metadata.Tafsir: (And thou art an indweller of this city) and it is also said that this means: Allah has made lawful for you in this city that which he did not make lawful to anyone before or after you; and it is also said that this means: you are excused regarding that which you do in this city.

translation: And you are free (from sin, and to punish the enemies of Islâm on the Day of the conquest) in this city (Makkah).

metadata.arabic: وَوَالِدٍ وَمَا وَلَدَ
metadata.Tafsir: (And the begetter and that which he begat) the begetter is Adam and that which his sons begat; and it is also said this means: the begetter refers to the person who can have children, whether this person is a man or a woman, while that which he begat refers to the men or women who cannot have children; Allah swore by all these,

translation: And by the begetter (i.e. Adam عليه السلام) and that which he begot (i.e. his progeny).

metadata.arabic: لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلإِنسَانَ فِي كَبَدٍ
metadata.Tafsir: (We verily have created man) i.e. Kildah Ibn Usayd (in an atmosphere) in an erect form; it is also said that this means: in strife with the matter of the life of this world and of the Hereafter; and it is also said this means: with strength and force:

translation: Verily, We have created man in toil.

metadata.arabic: أَيَحْسَبُ أَن لَّن يَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ أَحَدٌ
metadata.Tafsir: (Thinketh he) does the disbelieving man think (that) because of his strength and force (none hath power over him?) i.e. Allah cannot seize and punish him.

translation: Does he think that none can overcome him?

metadata.arabic: يَقُولُ أَهْلَكْتُ مَالاً لُّبَداً
metadata.Tafsir: (And he) Kildah Ibn Usayd; and it is also said: al-Walid Ibn al-Mughirah (saith: I have destroyed vast wealth) I have spent abundant wealth in enmity towards Muhammad, Allah bless him, and this did not benefit me:

translation: He says (boastfully): "I have wasted wealth in abundance!"

metadata.arabic: أَيَحْسَبُ أَن لَّمْ يَرَهُ أَحَدٌ
metadata.Tafsir: (Thinketh he) does the disbelieving man deem (that none beholdeth him) that Allah does not see his deeds whether he spends money or not?

translation: Does he think that none sees him?

metadata.arabic: أَلَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُ عَيْنَيْنِ
metadata.Tafsir: Allah then mentioned the blessings He bestowed upon him, saying: (Did We not assign unto him two eyes) with which he sees

translation: Have We not made for him two eyes,

metadata.arabic: وَلِسَاناً وَشَفَتَيْنِ
metadata.Tafsir: (And a tongue) with which he speaks (and two lips) which he can join together or separate,

translation: And a tongue and two lips?

metadata.arabic: وَهَدَيْنَاهُ ٱلنَّجْدَينِ
metadata.Tafsir: (And guide him to the parting of the mountain ways?) And We showed him the way of goodness and the way of evil; and it is also that this means: the way to the two breasts.

translation: And shown him the two ways (good and evil)?

metadata.arabic: فَلاَ ٱقتَحَمَ ٱلْعَقَبَةَ
metadata.Tafsir: (But he hath not attempted the Ascent) He says: but did he go beyond that hurdle which is the Bridge over hell?

translation: But he has not attempted to pass on the path that is steep (i.e. the path which will lead to goodness and success).

metadata.arabic: وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا ٱلْعَقَبَةُ
metadata.Tafsir: (Ah, what will convey unto thee) O Muhammad (what the Ascent is!) it is a smooth hurdle between Paradise and hell. Allah said this to arouse the Prophet's astonishment.

translation: And what will make you know the path that is steep?

metadata.arabic: فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ
metadata.Tafsir: ((It is) to free a slave) He says: its crossing requires the freeing of a slave; and it is also said this means: none will cross it save he who has freed a slave,

translation: (It is) freeing a neck (slave)

metadata.arabic: أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ
metadata.Tafsir: (And to feed in the day of hunger) and hardship

translation: Or giving food in a day of hunger (famine),

metadata.arabic: يَتِيماً ذَا مَقْرَبَةٍ
metadata.Tafsir: (An orphan near of kin,

translation: To an orphan near of kin.

metadata.arabic: أَوْ مِسْكِيناً ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ
metadata.Tafsir: Or some poor wretch in misery) and who has nothing,

translation: Or to a Miskîn (poor) cleaving to dust (out of misery).

metadata.arabic: ثُمَّ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بِٱلصَّبْرِ وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بِٱلْمَرْحَمَةِ
metadata.Tafsir: (And to be) in addition to this (of those who believe) in private between themselves and their Lord, in Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an (and exhort one another to perseverance) in fulfilling the obligations (and export one another to pity) towards the poor and needy.

translation: Then he became one of those who believed (in the Islamic Monotheism) and recommended one another to perseverance and patience, and (also) recommended one another to pity and compassion.

metadata.arabic: أُوْلَـٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَيْمَنَةِ
metadata.Tafsir: (Their place will be on the right hand) those who are given their register in their right hands are the inhabitants of the Garden.

translation: They are those on the Right Hand (i.e. the dwellers of Paradise),

metadata.arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِآيَاتِنَا هُمْ أَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَشْأَمَةِ
metadata.Tafsir: (But those who disbelieve Our revelations) in Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an, i.e. Kildah and his host, (their place will be on the left hand) those who are given their register in their left hand are the inhabitants of the Fire.

translation: But those who disbelieved in Our Ayât (proofs, evidence, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.), they are those on the Left Hand (the dwellers of Hell).

metadata.arabic: عَلَيْهِمْ نَارٌ مُّؤْصَدَةٌ
metadata.Tafsir: (Fire will be an awning over them) the Fire will fall on them'.

translation: The Fire will be shut over them (i.e. they will be enveloped by the Fire without any opening or window or outlet.

metadata.arabic: وَٱلشَّمْسِ وَضُحَاهَا
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (By the sun and his brightness): '(By the sun and his brightness) Allah swears by the sun and its light,

translation: By the sun and its brightness.

metadata.arabic: وَٱلْقَمَرِ إِذَا تَلاَهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (And the moon when she followeth him) when it follows the sun, on the first night when the new moon is seen,

translation: By the moon as it follows it (the sun).

metadata.arabic: وَٱلنَّهَارِ إِذَا جَلاَّهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (And the day when it revealeth him,

translation: By the day as it shows up (the sun’s) brightness.

metadata.arabic: وَٱللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَاهَا
metadata.Tafsir: And the night when it enshroudeth him) and the night when it enshrouds the light of day and the day reveals the darkness of the night,

translation: By the night as it conceals it (the sun).

metadata.arabic: وَٱلسَّمَآءِ وَمَا بَنَاهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (And the heaven and Him who built it) by Him Who created it, i.e. Allah, Allah swore by Himself,

translation: By the heaven and Him Who built it.

metadata.arabic: وَٱلأَرْضِ وَمَا طَحَاهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (And the earth and Him who spread it) over the water,

translation: By the earth and Him Who spread it.

metadata.arabic: وَنَفْسٍ وَمَا سَوَّاهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (And a soul and Him who perfected it) by creating it with two hands, two feet, two eyes, two ears as well as with all the other organs.

translation: By Nafs (Adam or a person or a soul), and Him Who perfected him in proportion;

metadata.arabic: فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَاهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (And inspired it (with conscience of) what is wrong for it and (what is) right for it) He made known to it and explained what it should go for and what it should avoid; Allah swore by all these things as well as by Himself.

translation: Then He showed him what is wrong for him and what is right for him.

metadata.arabic: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن زَكَّاهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (He is indeed successful who causeth it to grow) who refines it, makes things clear for it and guides it to success,

translation: Indeed he succeeds who purifies his ownself (i.e. obeys and performs all that Allâh ordered, by following the true Faith of Islâmic Monotheism and by doing righteous good deeds).

metadata.arabic: وَقَدْ خَابَ مَن دَسَّاهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (And he is indeed a failure) he is in loss (who stunteth it) who leads to sin, error and forsakenness.

translation: And indeed he fails who corrupts his ownself (i.e. disobeys what Allâh has ordered by rejecting the true Faith of Islâmic Monotheism or by following polytheism or by doing every kind of evil wicked deeds).

metadata.arabic: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِطَغْوَاهَآ
metadata.Tafsir: (The tribe of) Thamud) the folk of Salih (denied (the Truth) in their rebellious pride) He says: their transgression led them to this.

translation: Thamûd (people) denied (their Prophet) through their transgression (by rejecting the true Faith of Islâmic Monotheism, and by following polytheism, and by committing every kind of sin).

metadata.arabic: إِذِ ٱنبَعَثَ أَشْقَاهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (When the basest of them broke forth) when the most wretched of the folk, Qudar Ibn Salif and Masda', hamstrung the she-camel.

translation: When the most wicked man among them went forth (to kill the she-camel).

metadata.arabic: فَقَالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ نَاقَةَ ٱللَّهِ وَسُقْيَاهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (And the messenger of Allah) Salih (said) that is before they hamstrung the she-camel: (It is the she-camel of Allah) leave the she-camel of Allah alone, (so let her drink!) i.e. and let her drink in peace!

translation: But the Messenger of Allâh [Sâlih عليه السلام] said to them: "Be cautious! (Fear the evil end). That is the she-camel of Allâh! (Do not harm it) and bar it not from having its drink!"

metadata.arabic: فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَعَقَرُوهَا فَدَمْدَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ بِذَنبِهِمْ فَسَوَّاهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (But they denied him) they denied the message brought by Salih, (and they hamstrung her) they hamstrung the she-camel, (so Allah doomed them for their sin) so Allah destroyed them because of killing the she-camel and disbelieving in Salih (and razed (their dwellings)) killing the old and the young among them.

translation: Then they denied him and they killed it. So their Lord destroyed them because of their sin, and made them equal in destruction (i.e. all grades of people, rich and poor, strong and weak, etc.)!

metadata.arabic: وَلاَ يَخَافُ عُقْبَاهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (He dreadeth not the sequel (of events)) and it is also said this means: and He dreads not the one who instigated it'.

translation: And He (Allâh) feared not the consequences thereof.

metadata.arabic: وَٱلْلَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying: (By the night enshrouding): '(By the night enshrouding) He says: Allah swears by the night when it enshrouds the light of day.

translation: By the night as it envelops.

metadata.arabic: وَٱلنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (And the day resplendent) and the day when it clears the darkness of night.

translation: By the day as it appears in brightness.

metadata.arabic: وَمَا خَلَقَ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلأُنثَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (And Him Who hath created) and by Him Who has created the (male and female,

translation: By Him Who created male and female.

metadata.arabic: إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: Lo! your effort) your work (is dispersed (towards diverse ends)) there are those who oppose and disbelieve in Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an and there are those who believe in Muhammad (pbuh); there are those who strive for Paradise and there are those who strive for hell. This is why Allah made the oath.

translation: Certainly, your efforts and deeds are diverse (different in aims and purposes);

metadata.arabic: فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَعْطَىٰ وَٱتَّقَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (As for him who giveth) to charity from his wealth for the sake of Allah and bought nine believers who were in the hands of the disbelievers who tortured them to renounce their religion; this person bought them and then freed them (and is dutiful (towards Allah)) and wards off disbelief, idolatry and indecencies

translation: As for him who gives (in charity) and keeps his duty to Allâh and fears Him,

metadata.arabic: وَصَدَّقَ بِٱلْحُسْنَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (And believeth in goodness) and believes in Allah's provision; and it is also said this means: and believes in Paradise; and it is also said this means: and believes in " there is no deity save Allah " ;

translation: And believes in Al-Husnâ.

metadata.arabic: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Surely We will ease his way unto the state of ease) We shall make easy for him acts of obedience and give him success, time and again, to perform acts of obedience; and it is also said this means: We shall give him success, time and again, to give alms for the sake of Allah; this refers to Abu Bakr al-Siddiq.

translation: We will make smooth for him the path of ease (goodness).

metadata.arabic: وَأَمَّا مَن بَخِلَ وَٱسْتَغْنَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (But as for him who hoardeth) his wealth and is too stingy to give for the sake of Allah, in reference here to al-Walid Ibn al-Mughirah and it is said: Abu Sufyan Ibn Harb who was not a believer at that time (and deemeth himself independent) of Allah,

translation: But he who is greedy miser and thinks himself self-sufficient.

metadata.arabic: وَكَذَّبَ بِٱلْحُسْنَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (And disbelieveth in goodness) and disbelieves in Allah's provision; and it is also said: in Paradise; and it is also said: in " there is no deity save Allah " ;

translation: And belies Al-Husnâ (See the footnote of the Verse No.6)

metadata.arabic: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Surely We will ease his way unto adversity) We shall make easy for him acts of disobedience and refraining from giving to charity, time and again.

translation: We will make smooth for him the path for evil.

metadata.arabic: وَمَا يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مَالُهُ إِذَا تَرَدَّىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (His riches) which he amasses in the life of the world (will not save him when he perisheth) when he dies; and it is also said this means: when he is cast in the Fire.

translation: And what will his wealth avail him when he goes down (in destruction)?.

metadata.arabic: إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا لَلْهُدَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Lo! Ours it is (to give) the guidance) it is for Us to show what is good and what is evil

translation: Truly! On Us is (to give) guidance.

metadata.arabic: وَإِنَّ لَنَا لَلآخِرَةَ وَٱلأُولَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (And lo! unto Us belong the latter portion and the former) and to Us belong the reward of the life of the world and that of the Hereafter; it is also said that this means: to Us belong the life of the world in which We bestow knowledge and success and also the Hereafter in which We bestow reward and honour.

translation: And truly, unto Us (belong) the last (Hereafter) and the first (this world).

metadata.arabic: فَأَنذَرْتُكُمْ نَاراً تَلَظَّىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Therefore have I warned you) of people of Mecca by means of the Qur'an (of the flaming Fire

translation: Therefore I have warned you of a blazing Fire (Hell).

metadata.arabic: لاَ يَصْلَٰهَآ إِلاَّ ٱلأَشْقَى
metadata.Tafsir: Which only the most wretched must endure) which only the wretched, as in Allah's foreknowledge, will enter,

translation: None shall enter it save the most wretched.

metadata.arabic: ٱلَّذِي كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (He who denieth) Allah's divine Oneness; and it is also said: who falls short in obeying Allah (and turneth away) from faith; and it is also said: from repentance.

translation: Who denies and turns away.

metadata.arabic: وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا ٱلأَتْقَى
metadata.Tafsir: (Far removed from it) from the Fire (will be the righteous

translation: And Al-Muttaqûn (the pious - See V.2:2) will be far removed from it (Hell).

metadata.arabic: ٱلَّذِى يُؤْتِي مَالَهُ يَتَزَكَّىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: Who giveth his wealth) in the way of Allah, i.e. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (that he may grow (in goodness)) intending by that Allah's Countenance alone,

translation: He who spends his wealth for increase in self-purification,

metadata.arabic: وَمَا لأَحَدٍ عِندَهُ مِن نِّعْمَةٍ تُجْزَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (And none hath with him any favour for reward,

translation: And who has (in mind) no favour from anyone to be paid back,

metadata.arabic: إِلاَّ ٱبْتِغَآءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: Except as seeking (to fulfil) the purpose of his Lord Most High) except seeking the good pleasure of his Lord the Most High, Who is higher than everything.

translation: Except to seek the Countenance of his Lord, the Most High.

metadata.arabic: وَلَسَوْفَ يَرْضَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (He verily will be content) he will be given of reward and honour until he is pleased, i.e. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and his fellow believers'.

translation: He surely will be pleased (when he enters Paradise).

metadata.arabic: وَٱلضُّحَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said about the interpretation of Allah's saying (By the morning hours): '(By the morning hours) He says: Allah swears by the whole day

translation: By the forenoon (after sunrise).

metadata.arabic: وَٱللَّيْلِ إِذَا سَجَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (And by the night when it is stillest) and by the night when it becomes dark,

translation: By the night when it darkens (and stand still).

metadata.arabic: مَا وَدَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وَمَا قَلَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Thy Lord hath not forsaken thee) your Lord has not left you since He inspired you (nor doth He hate thee) since He loved you; this is the reason for Allah's oath, this was revealed after the revelations from Allah stopped for 15 nights because the Prophet (pbuh) forgot to say " if Allah wills " when he promised the idolaters to answer their questions. And because the revelations stopped for this period of time the idolaters said: the Lord of Prophet has forsaken him and He hates him.

translation: Your Lord (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) has neither forsaken you nor hates you.

metadata.arabic: وَلَلآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لَّكَ مِنَ ٱلأُولَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (And verily the latter portion will be better for thee than the former) He says: the reward of the Hereafter is better for you than the reward of the life of the world.

translation: And indeed the Hereafter is better for you than the present (life of this world).

metadata.arabic: وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (And verily thy Lord will give unto thee) in the Hereafter of intercession (so that thou wilt be content) until you are content.

translation: And verily, your Lord will give you (all good) so that you shall be well-pleased.

metadata.arabic: أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيماً فَآوَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: Allah then mentioned His blessings upon the Prophet (pbuh) saying (Did He not find thee) O Muhammad (an orphan) without a father or mother (and protect (thee)) and joined you to your uncle Abu Talib and sufficed you your provision? The Prophet (pbuh) said: " Yes, O Gabriel! "

translation: Did He not find you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) an orphan and gave you a refuge?

metadata.arabic: وَوَجَدَكَ ضَآلاًّ فَهَدَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: Gabriel then said: (Did He not find thee) O Muhammad (wandering) among people in error (and direct (thee)) and guided you by means of prophethood? The Prophet (pbuh) said: " Yes, O Gabriel! "

translation: And He found you unaware (of the Qur’ân, its laws, and Prophethood) and guided you?

metadata.arabic: وَوَجَدَكَ عَآئِلاً فَأَغْنَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: And he also said: (Did He not find thee) O Muhammad (destitute) poor (and enrich (thee)) with the wealth of Khadijah; and it is also said this means: and made you content with that which He gave you? The Prophet (pbuh) said: " Yes, O Gabriel! "

translation: And He found you poor and made you rich (self-sufficient with self-contentment)?

metadata.arabic: فَأَمَّا ٱلْيَتِيمَ فَلاَ تَقْهَرْ
metadata.Tafsir: So he also said: (Therefore the orphan oppress not) do not transgress on him nor deride him,

translation: Therefore, treat not the orphan with oppression.

metadata.arabic: وَأَمَّا ٱلسَّآئِلَ فَلاَ تَنْهَرْ
metadata.Tafsir: (Therefore the beggar drive not away) nor rebuke,

translation: And repulse not the beggar.

metadata.arabic: وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ
metadata.Tafsir: (Therefore of the bounty of thy Lord) through prophethood and Islam (be thy discourse) speak to people and let them know about it'.

translation: And proclaim the Grace of your Lord (i.e. the Prophethood and all other Graces).

metadata.arabic: أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said concerning the interpretation of Allah's saying (Have We not caused thy bosom to dilate): '(Have We not caused thy bosom to dilate) this is in conjunction with His saying (Did He not find thee destitute and enrich (thee)?), and so Allah says: did We not open your heart for Islam? i.e. did We not soften your heart on the Day of the Covenant through knowledge, understanding, help, reason and certainty, as well as with other things? It is also said this means: did We not expand your heart through prophethood? And the Prophet (pbuh) said: “Yes, indeed!”

translation: Have We not opened your breast for you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم)?

metadata.arabic: وَوَضَعْنَا عَنكَ وِزْرَكَ
metadata.Tafsir: He said again: (And eased thee of the burden) We lifted your sins from you

translation: And removed from you your burden.

metadata.arabic: ٱلَّذِيۤ أَنقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Which weighed down thy back?) It is also said: prophethood weighed down your back; And the Prophet (pbuh) said: " Yes, indeed! "

translation: Which weighed down your back?

metadata.arabic: وَرَفَعْنَا لَكَ ذِكْرَكَ
metadata.Tafsir: (And exalted thy fame) and raised your voice with the call to prayer, supplication and testification of faith, such that you are mentioned just as I am? And the Prophet (pbuh) said: " Yes, indeed! "

translation: And have We not raised high your fame?

metadata.arabic: فَإِنَّ مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْراً
metadata.Tafsir: Allah then said to comfort His prophet about his poverty and the hardships he faced, saying: (But lo! with hardship goeth ease,

translation: Verily, along with every hardship is relief,

metadata.arabic: إِنَّ مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْراً
metadata.Tafsir: Lo! with hardship goeth ease;

translation: Verily, along with every hardship is relief (i.e. there is one hardship with two reliefs, so one hardship cannot overcome two reliefs).

metadata.arabic: فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ فَٱنصَبْ
metadata.Tafsir: So when thou art relieved) when you finish from military expeditions, jihad and fighting, (still toil) in worship; and it is also said this means: when you finish from the prescribed prayers, make supplications

translation: So when you have finished (your occupation), devote yourself for Allâh’s worship.

metadata.arabic: وَإِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَٱرْغَبْ
metadata.Tafsir: (And strive to please thy Lord) and ask your needs from your Lord'.

translation: And to your Lord (Alone) turn (all your) intentions and hopes.

metadata.arabic: وَٱلتِّينِ وَٱلزَّيْتُونِ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (By the fig and the olive): '(By the fig and the olive) He says: Allah swears by the fig, this fig of yours, and the olive, this olive of yours; it is also said the fig and the olive refer to two mountains in Historic Syria; it is also said that the fig refers to the hill upon which Jerusalem is built while the olive refers to the mountain upon which Damascus is built,

translation: By the fig, and the olive.

metadata.arabic: وَطُورِ سِينِينَ
metadata.Tafsir: (By Mount Sinai) and He swears by the mountain of Thubayr which is the mountain of Midian where Allah spoke to Moses (pbuh),

translation: By Mount Sinai.

metadata.arabic: وَهَـٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدِ ٱلأَمِينِ
metadata.Tafsir: (And by this land made safe) and He swears by Mecca which is made safe in that whoever enters it is safe;

translation: By this city of security (Makkah).

metadata.arabic: لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلإِنسَانَ فِيۤ أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ
metadata.Tafsir: (Surely We created man) the disbelieving man, referring here to al-Walid Ibn al-Mughirah, and it is also said it refers to Kildah Ibn Usayd (of the best stature) in the best of forms; and this is the reason why the oath was made.

translation: Verily, We created man in the best stature (mould).

metadata.arabic: ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَاهُ أَسْفَلَ سَافِلِينَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Then We reduced him) in the Hereafter (to the lowest of the low) i.e. the Fire; it is also said that the above means: We have created the children of Adam in the best of forms when they are in the pick of their youth, then We reduce them to abject old age whereby no good deed is recorded in their favour except that which they used to do in their youth and prime,

translation: Then We reduced him to the lowest of the low.

metadata.arabic: إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ
metadata.Tafsir: (Save those who believe) in Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an (and do good works) and do acts of obedience in private between themselves and their Lord, (and theirs is a reward unfailing) their reward is undiminished and unspoilt, good deeds will still be written for them even in old age and after they die.

translation: Save those who believe (in Islâmic Monotheism) and do righteous deeds. Then they shall have a reward without end (Paradise).

metadata.arabic: فَمَا يُكَذِّبُكَ بَعْدُ بِٱلدِّينِ
metadata.Tafsir: (So who henceforth) i.e. after what I have mentioned to you of the transformation of youth and old age, life and death (will give the lie to thee) O Muhammad (about the judgement) about the Day of Reckoning? It is also said this means: what has driven you, O Kildah Ibn Usayd and Walid Ibn al-Mughirah, to deny the Day of Judgement?

translation: Then what (or who) causes you (O disbelievers) to deny the Recompense (i.e. the Day of Resurrection)?

metadata.arabic: أَلَيْسَ ٱللَّهُ بِأَحْكَمِ ٱلْحَاكِمِينَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Is not Allah the most conclusive of all judges?) Is not Allah the most just of those who are just and the best of those who are best and is, therefore, able to bring you back to life, O Walid!'

translation: Is not Allâh the Best of judges?

metadata.arabic: ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (Read): '(Read) He says: Read, O Muhammad, the Qur'an; this is the first revelation that Gabriel brought down: (In the name of thy Lord) by the command of your Lord (Who createth) the created beings,

translation: Read! In the Name of your Lord Who has created (all that exists).

metadata.arabic: خَلَقَ ٱلإِنسَانَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ
metadata.Tafsir: (Createth man) i.e. the son of Adam (from a clot) and the Prophet (pbuh) said: “what shall I read?” And Gabriel read to him the first four verses of this surah.

translation: He has created man from a clot (a piece of thick coagulated blood).

metadata.arabic: ٱقْرَأْ وَرَبُّكَ ٱلأَكْرَمُ
metadata.Tafsir: He said to him: (Read) the Qur'an, O Muhammad: (And thy Lord is the Most Bounteous) and your Lord is Clement and forgives the ignorance of the servants,

translation: Read! And your Lord is the Most Generous.

metadata.arabic: ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَ بِٱلْقَلَمِ
metadata.Tafsir: (Who teacheth by the pen) Who teaches writing by the pen,

translation: Who has taught (the writing) by the pen.

metadata.arabic: عَلَّمَ ٱلإِنسَانَ مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ
metadata.Tafsir: (Teacheth man) writing with the pen (that which be knew not) before this; it is also said: He taught man the names of all things which he previously did not know.

translation: He has taught man that which he knew not.

metadata.arabic: كَلاَّ إِنَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ لَيَطْغَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Nay, but verily) O Muhammad (man) i.e. the disbeliever (is rebellious) is a wanton, he moves from one position to another with regard to his food, drink, clothing and mount

translation: Nay! Verily, man does transgress (in disbelief and evil deed).

metadata.arabic: أَن رَّآهُ ٱسْتَغْنَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (That he thinketh himself independent) of Allah because of his wealth!

translation: Because he considers himself self-sufficient.

metadata.arabic: إِنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلرُّجْعَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Lo! unto thy Lord) O Muhammad (is the return) of all created beings in the Hereafter.

translation: Surely, unto your Lord is the return.

metadata.arabic: أَرَأَيْتَ ٱلَّذِي يَنْهَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: Then it was revealed about Abu Jahl Ibn Hisham when he wanted to step on the neck of the Prophet (pbuh) while he was in prayer: (Hast thou seen him) O Muhammad (who dissuadeth

translation: Have you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) seen him (i.e. Abû Jahl) who prevents

metadata.arabic: عَبْداً إِذَا صَلَّىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: A slave) i.e. Muhammad (pbuh) (when he prayeth) to Allah?

translation: A slave (Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) when he prays?

metadata.arabic: أَرَأَيْتَ إِن كَانَ عَلَىٰ ٱلْهُدَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Hast thou seen if he (relieth) on the guidance (of Allah)) i.e. Muhammad (pbuh) is following the guidance: prophethood and Islam

translation: Tell me if he (Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) is on the guidance (of Allâh)

metadata.arabic: أَوْ أَمَرَ بِٱلتَّقْوَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Or enjoineth piety) and enjoins belief in Allah's divine Oneness?

translation: Or enjoins piety!

metadata.arabic: أَرَأَيْتَ إِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Hast thou seen if he denieth (Allah's guidance)) and Abu Jahl disbelieved in Allah's divine Oneness (and is froward) and turned away from faith?

translation: Tell me if he (Abû Jahl) denies (the truth, i.e. this Qur’ân) and turns away?

metadata.arabic: أَلَمْ يَعْلَم بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرَىٰ
metadata.Tafsir: (Is he) Abu Jahl (then unaware that Allah seeth) what he did to the Prophet (pbuh)?

translation: Knows he not that Allâh does see (what he does)?

metadata.arabic: كَلاَّ لَئِن لَّمْ يَنتَهِ لَنَسْفَعاً بِٱلنَّاصِيَةِ
metadata.Tafsir: (Nay) truly, O Muhammad, (but if he cease not) if Abu Jahl does not repent of harming the Prophet (pbuh). (We will seize him by the forelock

translation: Nay! If he (Abû Jahl) ceases not, We will catch him by the forelock -

metadata.arabic: نَاصِيَةٍ كَاذِبَةٍ خَاطِئَةٍ
metadata.Tafsir: The lying) about Allah, (sinful forelock) that ascribes partners to Allah

translation: A lying, sinful forelock!

metadata.arabic: فَلْيَدْعُ نَادِيَهُ
metadata.Tafsir: (Then let him call upon his henchmen) his folk and companions!

translation: Then let him call upon his council (of helpers).

metadata.arabic: سَنَدْعُ ٱلزَّبَانِيَةَ
metadata.Tafsir: (We will call the guards of hell) i.e. the keepers of hell.

translation: We will call out the guards of Hell (to deal with him)!

metadata.arabic: كَلاَّ لاَ تُطِعْهُ وَٱسْجُدْ وَٱقْتَرِب
metadata.Tafsir: (Nay) truly, O Muhammad! (Obey not thou him) i.e. obey not Abu Jahl when he wants you not to pray to your Lord. (But prostrate thyself) to your Lord, (and draw near (unto Allah)) through prostration.

translation: Nay! (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم)! Do not obey him (Abû Jahl). Fall prostrate and draw near to Allâh!

metadata.arabic: إِنَّا أَنزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةِ ٱلْقَدْرِ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (Lo! We revealed it): '(Lo! We revealed it) He says: We sent Gabriel with the entire Qur'an to the scribes of the nether heaven (on the Night of Power) on the night of judgement and decree; it is also said this means: on a night blessed with forgiveness and mercy, and then it was revealed to the Prophet (pbuh) in instalments.

translation: Verily, We have sent it (this Qur’ân) down in the night of Al-Qadr (Decree).

metadata.arabic: وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ
metadata.Tafsir: (Ah, what will convey unto thee) O Muhammad-this is said out of glorification of this night-(what the Night of Power is) what the merit of the Night of Power is!

translation: And what will make you know what the night of Al-Qadr (Decree) is?

metadata.arabic: لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ
metadata.Tafsir: He then explained its merit by saying: (The Night of Power is better than a thousand months) He says: works in this night are better than works performed in 1,000 months which do not include such a night.

translation: The night of Al-Qadr (Decree) is better than a thousand months (i.e. worshipping Allâh in that night is better than worshipping Him a thousand months, i.e. 83 years and 4 months).

metadata.arabic: تَنَزَّلُ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ فِيهَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِم مِّن كُلِّ أَمْرٍ
metadata.Tafsir: (The angels and the Spirit) Gabriel with them (descend therein) at the beginning of the Night of Power, (by the permission of their Lord) by the command of their Lord, (with all decrees.

translation: Therein descend the angels and the Rûh [Jibrîl (Gabrîl)] by Allâh’s Permission with all Decrees,

metadata.arabic: سَلاَمٌ هِيَ حَتَّىٰ مَطْلَعِ ٱلْفَجْرِ
metadata.Tafsir: (That night is) Peace) He says: they greet the greeting of peace those who fast and those who pray, on that day, from among the nation of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) (until the rising of the dawn) He says: its merit and grace lasts until the rise of dawn'.

translation: (All that night), there is Peace (and Goodness from Allâh to His believing slaves) until the appearance of dawn.

metadata.arabic: لَمْ يَكُنِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ وَٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ مُنفَكِّينَ حَتَّىٰ تَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلْبَيِّنَةُ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (Those who disbelieve among the People of the Scripture): '(Those who disbelieve among the People of the Scripture) i.e. the Jews and Christians (and the idolaters) the Arab idolaters (could not have left off (erring)) could not have remained in their denial of Muhammad (pbuh) the Qur'an and Islam (till the clear proof came unto them) until clarification of what is in their Scriptures, the Scriptures of the Jews and Christians, came to them. There is another way of understanding the above: those who disbelieve among the people of the Scripture, before the advent Muhammad (pbuh) such as 'Abdullah Ibn Salam and his followers, and those who ascribed partners to Allah before the advent of Muhammad (pbuh) such as Abu Bakr and his fellow Arabs, would not have desisted from their disbelief and idolatry until the clear proof came to them, i.e. until Muhammad (pbuh) came to them.

translation: Those who disbelieve from among the people of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) and Al-Mushrikûn, were not going to leave (their disbelief) until there came to them clear evidence.

metadata.arabic: رَسُولٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ يَتْلُواْ صُحُفاً مُّطَهَّرَةً
metadata.Tafsir: (A messenger from Allah) i.e. Muhammad (pbuh) (reading) to them (purified pages) pages purified from idolatry

translation: A Messenger (Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) from Allâh, reciting (the Qur’ân) purified pages [purified from Al-Bâtil (falsehood)].

metadata.arabic: فِيهَا كُتُبٌ قَيِّمَةٌ
metadata.Tafsir: (Containing) i.e. the page of Muhammad (pbuh) contains (correct scriptures) a religion and a straight and just way that contains no crookedness.

translation: Wherein are correct and straight laws from Allâh.

metadata.arabic: وَمَا تَفَرَّقَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ إِلاَّ مِن بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَتْهُمُ ٱلْبَيِّنَةُ
metadata.Tafsir: (Nor were the People of the Scripture divided) those who were given the Torah, i.e. Ka'b Ibn al-Ashraf and his host, did not differ about Muhammad (pbuh) the Qur'an and Islam (until after the clear proof came unto them) until the clarification of what is in their Scripture regarding the traits and description of Muhammad (pbuh) came to them.

translation: And the people of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) differed not until after there came to them clear evidence (i.e. Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم and whatever was revealed to him).

metadata.arabic: وَمَآ أُمِرُوۤاْ إِلاَّ لِيَعْبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ ٱلدِّينَ حُنَفَآءَ وَيُقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلاَةَ وَيُؤْتُواْ ٱلزَّكَاةَ وَذَلِكَ دِينُ ٱلقَيِّمَةِ
metadata.Tafsir: (And they are ordered) in all the Scriptures (naught else than to serve Allah) nothing else but to profess Allah's divine Oneness, (keeping religion pure for Him) through the profession of Allah's divine Oneness, (as men by nature upright) as ones surrendered unto Him, (and to establish worship) and perform the five daily prayers after declaring their profession in Allah's divine Oneness (and to pay the poor-due) from their wealth after that. Allah then mentioned belief in Allah's divine Oneness, saying: (That) i.e. belief in Allah's divine Oneness (is true religion) the religion of truth, straight without any crookedness; it is also said that this means: that, i.e. belief in Allah's divine Oneness, is the religion of the angels; and it is also said this means: it is the religion of those who are by nature upright; and it is also said this means: the religion of Abraham.

translation: And they were commanded not, but that they should worship Allâh, and worship none but Him Alone (abstaining from ascribing partners to Him), and perform As-Salât (Iqâmat-as-Salât) and give Zakât, and that is the right religion.

metadata.arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ وَٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمْ شَرُّ ٱلْبَرِيَّةِ
metadata.Tafsir: (Lo! those who disbelieve) in Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an, (among the People of the Scripture and the idolaters) i.e. the idolaters among the people of Mecca, (will abide in fire of hell) never to die therein or leave it. (They are the worst of created beings.

translation: Verily, those who disbelieve (in the religion of Islâm, the Qur’ân and Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) from among the people of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) and Al-Mushrikûn will abide in the Fire of Hell. They are the worst of creatures.

metadata.arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ أُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمْ خَيْرُ ٱلْبَرِيَّةِ
metadata.Tafsir: (And) lo! those who believe) in Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an, such as 'Abdullah Ibn Salam and his followers and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and his companions (and do good works) acts of obedience privately between themselves and their Lord (are the best of created beings.

translation: Verily, those who believe [in the Oneness of Allâh, and in His Messenger Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) including all obligations ordered by Islâm] and do righteous good deeds, they are the best of creatures.

metadata.arabic: جَزَآؤُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِى مِنْ تَحْتِهَا ٱلأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَداً رِّضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُواْ عَنْهُ ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِيَ رَبَّهُ
metadata.Tafsir: Their reward is with their Lord: Gardens of Eden) the chamber of the Beneficent, the source of the prophets and those near to Him (beneath which) beneath whose trees, habitations and rooms (rivers flow) rivers of wine, water, honey and milk, (wherein they dwell forever) they remain in Paradise for ever never to die or leave it. (Allah hath pleasure in them) i.e. in their faith and works (and they have pleasure in Him) in His reward and bestowal of honour upon Him. (This) i.e. the Gardens and good pleasure (is (in store) for him who feareth his Lord) is for him who believes in Allah's divine Oneness such as Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and his companions and 'Abdullah Ibn Salam and his followers'.

translation: Their reward with their Lord is ‘Adn (Eden) Paradise (Gardens of Eternity), underneath which rivers flow. They will abide therein forever, Allâh will be pleased with them, and they with Him. That is for him who fears his Lord.

metadata.arabic: إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ ٱلأَرْضُ زِلْزَالَهَا
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said about the interpretation of Allah's saying (When Earth is shaken with her (final) earthquake): '(When Earth is shaken with her (final) earthquake) He says: the earth is shaken and quaking and all that which is on it of trees, mountains and building is crumbling down

translation: When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake.

metadata.arabic: وَأَخْرَجَتِ ٱلأَرْضُ أَثْقَالَهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (And Earth yieldeth up her burdens) and the Earth brings out her dead and treasures,

translation: And when the earth throws out its burdens.

metadata.arabic: وَقَالَ ٱلإِنسَانُ مَا لَهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (And man) i.e. the disbeliever (saith: What aileth her?) He says this in astonishment from the horror he sees

translation: And man will say: "What is the matter with it?"

metadata.arabic: يَوْمَئِذٍ تُحَدِّثُ أَخْبَارَهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (That day) when the earth is shaken (she will relate her chronicles) the earth will inform about the good and evil that were done on its surface,

translation: That Day it will declare its information (about all that happened over it of good or evil).

metadata.arabic: بِأَنَّ رَبَّكَ أَوْحَىٰ لَهَا
metadata.Tafsir: (Because thy Lord inspires her) because your Lord gives her leave to talk.

translation: Because your Lord will inspire it.

metadata.arabic: يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصْدُرُ ٱلنَّاسُ أَشْتَاتاً لِّيُرَوْاْ أَعْمَالَهُمْ
metadata.Tafsir: (That day) when the earth speaks (mankind will issue forth in scattered groups) a group will go to Paradise, these are the believers, and a group will go to hell, and these are the disbelievers (to be shown their deeds) what they have done of good or evil when they were in the life of the world.

translation: That Day mankind will proceed in scattered groups that they may be shown their deeds.

metadata.arabic: فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْراً يَرَهُ
metadata.Tafsir: Allah then revealed the following verse about a group of people who thought that they are not rewarded for any small goodness they do nor punished for any small evil they commit, and so Allah urged them to do acts of goodness even if they are small and warned them against acts of evil even if they are small acts: (And whoso doeth good an atom's weight) the weight of the smallest ant (will see it then) in his register and then will be happy with it; it is also said: the believer sees his works in the Hereafter while the disbeliever sees his works in the life of the world,

translation: So whosoever does good equal to the weight of an atom (or a small ant) shall see it.

metadata.arabic: وَمَن يَعْـمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرّاً يَرَهُ
metadata.Tafsir: (And whoso doeth ill an atom's weight) the weight of a small atom (will see it then) is written in his register and will displease him; and it is also said: the believer sees it in the life of the world while the disbeliever sees it in the Hereafter'.

translation: And whosoever does evil equal to the weight of an atom (or a small ant) shall see it.

metadata.arabic: وَٱلْعَادِيَاتِ ضَبْحاً
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said about the interpretation of Allah's saying (By the snorting courses): '(By the snorting courses) the Prophet (pbuh) had sent a military expedition to Banu Kinanah and was quite aggrieved because he did not hear their news for a while. Allah therefore informed His Prophet about this expedition in the form of an oath, saying (By the snorting courses) He says: Allah swears by the horses of the conquerors, whose breaths are audible because of the enemies,

translation: By the (steeds) that run, with panting.

metadata.arabic: فَٱلمُورِيَاتِ قَدْحاً
metadata.Tafsir: (Striking sparks of fire) with their hooves, but this fire is as beneficial as the Fire of Abu Hubahib. The latter was one of the stingiest Arabs in camp. He never lit any fire to make bread for himself or for anyone else until everybody went to sleep, and whenever someone woke up he hurried to put the Fire out so that no one would benefit from it.

translation: Striking sparks of fire (by their hooves).

metadata.arabic: فَٱلْمُغِيرَاتِ صُبْحاً
metadata.Tafsir: (And scouring to the raid at dawn,

translation: And scouring to the raid at dawn.

metadata.arabic: فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِ نَقْعاً
metadata.Tafsir: Then, therewith, with their trail of dust,

translation: And raise the dust in clouds the while.

metadata.arabic: فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعاً
metadata.Tafsir: Cleaving, as one, the centre (of the foe)) the above can also be understood as follow: Allah swears by the pilgrims' horses and camels when they return from 'Arafah to Muzdalifah snorting and striking sparks of fire; it is also said the latter means: performing acts which leads them to safety, i.e. the pilgrimage. And He swears by these when they go at dawn from Muzdalifah to Mina in the evening, leaving trails of dust and surrounding their enemies. Allah swore by all these.

translation: And penetrating forthwith as one into the midst (of the foe).

metadata.arabic: إِنَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ
metadata.Tafsir: (Lo! Man) i.e. the disbelieving man: Qurt Ibn 'Abdullah Ibn 'Amr; and it is also said it refers to Abu Hubahib (is an ingrate unto his Lord) He says: he is ungrateful for the blessings of his Lord; it is also said this means: He is disobedient of his Lord; and it is also said this means: he is stingy; and it is also said this means: he denies those who are dependent on him, starves his slaves, eats alone and does not give those who are his relatives among his folk.

translation: Verily, man (disbeliever) is ungrateful to his Lord.

metadata.arabic: وَإِنَّهُ عَلَىٰ ذَلِكَ لَشَهِيدٌ
metadata.Tafsir: (And lo! he is a witness unto that) and Allah records His doing;

translation: And to that he bears witness (by his deeds).

metadata.arabic: وَإِنَّهُ لِحُبِّ ٱلْخَيْرِ لَشَدِيدٌ
metadata.Tafsir: (And lo! in the love of wealth) abundant wealth (he) i.e. Qurt (is violent) is extreme.

translation: And verily, he is violent in the love of wealth.

metadata.arabic: أَفَلاَ يَعْلَمُ إِذَا بُعْثِرَ مَا فِي ٱلْقُبُورِ
metadata.Tafsir: (Knoweth he not) i.e. Abu Hubahib; and it is also said: Qurt (that, when the contents of the graves) the dead (are poured forth

translation: Knows he not that when the contents of the graves are poured forth (all mankind is resurrected)?

metadata.arabic: وَحُصِّلَ مَا فِي ٱلصُّدُورِ
metadata.Tafsir: And the secrets of the breasts) what is in the hearts of good and evil, miserliness and generosity (are made known.

translation: And that which is in the breasts (of men) is made known?

metadata.arabic: إِنَّ رَبَّهُم بِهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَّخَبِيرٌ
metadata.Tafsir: On that day) the Day of Judgement (will their Lord be perfectly informed concerning them) their Lord is perfectly Aware'.

translation: Verily, that Day (i.e. the Day of Resurrection) their Lord will be Well-Acquainted with them (as to their deeds and will reward them for their deeds).

metadata.arabic: ٱلْقَارِعَةُ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (Calamity! What is the Calamity?): '(Calamity!

translation: Al-Qâri‘ah (the striking Hour i.e. the Day of Resurrection).

metadata.arabic: مَا ٱلْقَارِعَةُ
metadata.Tafsir: What is the Calamity?) He says: the Hour! What is the Hour? He said this to arouse his wonder; the Hour is called Calamity because it shakes people's hearts.

translation: What is the striking (Hour)?

metadata.arabic: وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا ٱلْقَارِعَةُ
metadata.Tafsir: (Ah, what will convey unto thee) O Muhammad (what the Calamity is!) he said this to show its tremendousness.

translation: And what will make you know what the striking (Hour) is?

metadata.arabic: يَوْمَ يَكُونُ ٱلنَّاسُ كَٱلْفَرَاشِ ٱلْمَبْثُوثِ
metadata.Tafsir: Allah then gave more details about it, saying: (A day wherein mankind will be) a day when people will fall on each other (as thickly scattered moths

translation: It is a Day whereon mankind will be like moths scattered about.

metadata.arabic: وَتَكُونُ ٱلْجِبَالُ كَٱلْعِهْنِ ٱلْمَنفُوشِ
metadata.Tafsir: And the mountains will become as carded wool.

translation: And the mountains will be like carded wool.

metadata.arabic: فَأَمَّا مَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ
metadata.Tafsir: Then, as for him whose scales are heavy (with good works)) as for him whose good works weigh heavy on his scale; this refers to the believer,

translation: Then as for him whose balance (of good deeds) will be heavy,

metadata.arabic: فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَّاضِيَةٍ
metadata.Tafsir: (He will live a pleasant life) He will be in a pleasant Paradise, pleasing to himself.

translation: He will live a pleasant life (in Paradise).

metadata.arabic: وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَازِينُهُ
metadata.Tafsir: (But as for him whose scales are light) i.e. the disbeliever,

translation: But as for him whose balance (of good deeds) will be light,

metadata.arabic: فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ
metadata.Tafsir: (The Bereft and Hungry One will be his mother) his abode and destination will be the Fire; it is also said this means: he will be thrown in the Fire.

translation: He will have his home in Hâwiyah (pit, i.e. Hell).

metadata.arabic: وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا هِيَهْ
metadata.Tafsir: (Ah, what will convey unto thee) O Muhammad (what she is!) this is to show how tremendous she is,

translation: And what will make you know what it is?

metadata.arabic: نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌ
metadata.Tafsir: (Raging fire) extremely hot'.

translation: (It is) a fiercely blazing Fire!

metadata.arabic: أَلْهَاكُمُ ٱلتَّكَّاثُرُ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said about the interpretation of Allah's saying (Rivalry in worldly increase distracteth you): '(Rivalry in worldly increase distracteth you) He says: bragging about your status and lineage has distracted you

translation: The mutual rivalry (for piling up of worldly things) diverts you,

metadata.arabic: حَتَّىٰ زُرْتُمُ ٱلْمَقَابِرَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Until ye come to the graves) this is because the Banu Sahm and Banu 'Abd Manaf were bragging to each other about which tribe is larger as concerns the number of its population, and found out that the Banu 'Abd Manaf were more numerous. The Banu Sahm said at that point: “We were rooted out by injustice in the pagan era; go and count the living and the dead of our people and the living and the dead of your people”. When they did so they found out that the Banu Sahm were more numerous. Therefore the above verses were revealed about them: bragging about status and lineage distracted you to the extent that you visited the graveyards to count the dead; it is also said that this means: increase in wealth and children distracts you until you die and be put in the graves.

translation: Until you visit the graves (i.e. till you die).

metadata.arabic: كَلاَّ سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Nay) this is a reply and threat to them, (but ye will come to know) what will be done to you in the graves!

translation: Nay! You shall come to know!

metadata.arabic: ثُمَّ كَلاَّ سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Nay, but ye will come to know!) what will be done to you when you die!

translation: Again nay! You shall come to know!

metadata.arabic: كَلاَّ لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عِلْمَ ٱلْيَقِينِ
metadata.Tafsir: (Nay, would that ye knew (now)) what will be done to you on the Day of Judgement (with a sure knowledge!) what you bragged about in the life of the world!

translation: Nay! If you knew with a sure knowledge (the end result of piling up, you would not have been occupied yourselves in worldly things).

metadata.arabic: لَتَرَوُنَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ
metadata.Tafsir: (For ye will behold hellfire) on the Day of Judgement.

translation: Verily, You shall see the blazing Fire (Hell)!

metadata.arabic: ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّهَا عَيْنَ ٱلْيَقِينِ
metadata.Tafsir: (Aye, ye will behold it with sure vision) which cannot be missed on the Day of Judgement.

translation: And again, you shall see it with certainty of sight!

metadata.arabic: ثُمَّ لَتُسْأَلُنَّ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ
metadata.Tafsir: (Then, on that day) on the Day of Judgement, (ye will be asked concerning pleasure) you will be asked about whether you gave thanks for all the bounties you enjoyed, of food, drink, clothing, etc'.

translation: Then on that Day you shall be asked about the delights (you indulged in, in this world)!

metadata.arabic: وَٱلْعَصْرِ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said about the interpretation of Allah's saying (By the declining day): (By the declining day) Allah swears by the 'Asr prayer; and it is also said by the hardships of time,

translation: By Al-‘Asr (the time).

metadata.arabic: إِنَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ
metadata.Tafsir: (Lo! Man) i.e. the disbelieving man (is in a state of loss) and torment because of losing his family and position in Paradise; it is also said this means: he is in a state of loss because of decrease in his works in old age and its cessation after death,

translation: Verily, man is in loss,

metadata.arabic: إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بِٱلصَّبْرِ
metadata.Tafsir: (Save those who believe) in Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an (and do good works) and do acts of obedience privately between them and their Lord, (and exhort one another to truth) to belief in Allah's divine Oneness; and it is said to the Qur'an (and exhort one another to endurance) in performing the obligations imposed by Allah and in avoiding transgressions and also in enduring misfortunes and calamities, because the believers are unlike the disbelievers'.

translation: Except those who believe (in Islâmic Monotheism) and do righteous good deeds, and recommend one another to the truth [i.e. order one another to perform all kinds of good deeds (Al-Ma‘ruf) which Allâh has ordained, and abstain from all kinds of sins and evil deeds (Al-Munkar which Allâh has forbidden], and recommend one another to patience (for the sufferings, harms, and injuries which one may encounter in Allâh’s Cause during preaching His religion of Islâmic Monotheism or Jihâd).

metadata.arabic: ويْلٌ لِّكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُّمَزَةٍ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said about the interpretation of Allah's saying (Woe): '(Woe) severe punishment; and it is also said that this refers to a valley in Gehenna which is full of blood and puss; and it is also said that it refers to a well in the Fire (unto every slandering) who backbites people (traducer) and slanders and abuses them in their face. This verses was revealed about Akhnas Ibn Shurayq, or al-Walid Ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi, who used to backbite the Prophet (pbuh) and also abuse him when in his presence.

translation: Woe to every slanderer and backbiter.

metadata.arabic: ٱلَّذِى جَمَعَ مَالاً وَعَدَّدَهُ
metadata.Tafsir: (Who hath gathered wealth (of this world) and arranged it) and counted it; and it is also said: counted his camels.

translation: Who has gathered wealth and counted it.

metadata.arabic: يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ
metadata.Tafsir: (He) the disbeliever (thinketh that his wealth will render him immortal) in the life of the world.

translation: He thinks that his wealth will make him last forever!

metadata.arabic: كَلاَّ لَيُنبَذَنَّ فِي ٱلْحُطَمَةِ
metadata.Tafsir: (Nay) this is a reply to him: it will not render him immortal in the life of the world, (but verily he will be flung to the Consuming One.

translation: Nay! Verily, he will be thrown into the crushing Fire.

metadata.arabic: وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا ٱلْحُطَمَةُ
metadata.Tafsir: Ah, what will convey unto thee) O Muhammad (what the Consuming One is!) He said this to show its tremendousness.

translation: And what will make you know what the crushing Fire is?

metadata.arabic: نَارُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمُوقَدَةُ
metadata.Tafsir: Then He explained, saying: ((It is) the Fire of Allah, kindled) for the disbelievers,

translation: The fire of Allâh kindled,

metadata.arabic: ٱلَّتِي تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى ٱلأَفْئِدَةِ
metadata.Tafsir: (Which leapeth up over the hearts (of men)) which consumes everything until it reaches the hearts.

translation: Which leaps up over the hearts,

metadata.arabic: إِنَّهَا عَلَيْهِم مُّؤْصَدَةٌ
metadata.Tafsir: (Lo! It) i.e. the Fire (is closed in on them) on the disbelievers

translation: Verily, it shall be closed upon them,

metadata.arabic: فِي عَمَدٍ مُّمَدَّدَةِ
metadata.Tafsir: (In outstretched columns) it is also said that this means: its bottom is very deep'.

translation: In pillars stretched forth (i.e. they will be punished in the Fire with pillars).

metadata.arabic: أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأَصْحَابِ ٱلْفِيلِ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said about the interpretation of Allah's saying (Hast thou not seen): '(Hast thou not seen) i.e. have you not been informed, O Muhammad, in the Qur'an (how thy Lord dealt with) how your Lord punished and destroyed (the owners of the Elephant) the people of the Negus who intended to destroy the House of Allah?

translation: Have you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) not seen how your Lord dealt with the owners of the Elephant? [The Elephant army which came from Yemen under the command of Abrahah Al-Ashram intending to destroy the Ka‘bah at Makkah].

metadata.arabic: أَلَمْ يَجْعَلْ كَيْدَهُمْ فِي تَضْلِيلٍ
metadata.Tafsir: (Did He not bring their stratagem) their scheming (to naught) to utter loss,

translation: Did He not make their plot go astray?

metadata.arabic: وَأَرْسَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ طَيْراً أَبَابِيلَ
metadata.Tafsir: (And send against them) and set on them (swarms of flying creatures) in succession,

translation: And He sent against them birds, in flocks,

metadata.arabic: تَرْمِيهِم بِحِجَارَةٍ مِّن سِجِّيلٍ
metadata.Tafsir: (Which pelted them with) which threw on them (stones of baked clay) like baked bricks.

translation: Striking them with stones of Sijjîl (baked clay).

metadata.arabic: فَجَعَلَهُمْ كَعَصْفٍ مَّأْكُولٍ
metadata.Tafsir: (And made them like green crops devoured) by worms?'

translation: And He made them like (an empty field of) stalks (of which the corn has been eaten up by cattle).

metadata.arabic: لإِيلاَفِ قُرَيْشٍ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said about the interpretation of Allah's saying (For the taming of Quraysh): '(For the taming of Quraysh) he says: command Quraysh to be tamed to Allah's divine Oneness; and it is also said this means: mention My blessings to Quraysh so that they be tamed to Allah's divine Oneness.

translation: (It is a great Grace from Allâh) for the protection of the Quraish,

metadata.arabic: إِيلاَفِهِمْ رِحْلَةَ ٱلشِّتَآءِ وَٱلصَّيْفِ
metadata.Tafsir: (For their taming (We cause)) as We have tamed (the caravans to set forth in winter and summer) the caravans to set forth in winter to Yemen and in summer to Historic Syria; it is also said that this means: belief in Allah's divine Oneness is not hard for Quraysh just as their winter and summer trips are not hard for them.

translation: (And with all those Allâh’s Grace and Protections, We cause) the (Quraish) caravans to set forth safe in winter (to the south) and in summer (to the north without any fear),

metadata.arabic: فَلْيَعْبُدُواْ رَبَّ هَـٰذَا ٱلْبَيْتِ
metadata.Tafsir: (So let them worship) so let Quraysh declare the divine Oneness of (the Lord of this House) of the Lord of the Ka'bah,

translation: So let them worship (Allâh) the Lord of this House (the Ka‘bah in Makkah),

metadata.arabic: ٱلَّذِيۤ أَطْعَمَهُم مِّن جُوعٍ وَآمَنَهُم مِّنْ خَوْفٍ
metadata.Tafsir: (Who hath fed them against hunger) which lasted seven years; and it is also said this means: Who sufficed them the burden of hunger and travelling in winter and summer, because they used to make two trips a year, one in winter to Yemen and one in summer to Historic Syria, and so Allah sufficed them the burden of doing so (and hath made them safe from fear) of the enemy lest he attacks them; and it is also said: from the fear of the Negus and his host who wanted to destroy the Ka'bah; this surah is also in conjunction with the previous surah'.

translation: (He) Who has fed them against hunger, and has made them safe from fear.

metadata.arabic: أَرَأَيْتَ ٱلَّذِي يُكَذِّبُ بِٱلدِّينِ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (Hast thou observed him who belieth religion?): '(Hast thou observed him who belieth religion?) And it is said this means: have you observed him who belies the Day of Reckoning? This is in reference to 'As Ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi.

translation: Have you seen him who denies the Recompense?

metadata.arabic: فَذَلِكَ ٱلَّذِي يَدُعُّ ٱلْيَتِيمَ
metadata.Tafsir: (That is he who repelleth the orphan) from his own right; and it is also said this means: he denies the orphan his right,

translation: That is he who repulses the orphan (harshly),

metadata.arabic: وَلاَ يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلْمِسْكِينِ
metadata.Tafsir: (And urgeth not) nor observe (the feeding of the needy) giving alms to the needy.

translation: And urges not on the feeding of Al-Miskîn (the poor),

metadata.arabic: فَوَيْلٌ لِّلْمُصَلِّينَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Ah, woe) severe torment in the Fire (unto worshippers) unto the hypocrites

translation: So woe unto those performers of Salât (prayers) (hypocrites),

metadata.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَن صَلاَتِهِمْ سَاهُونَ
metadata.Tafsir: Allah then explained who they are by saying: (Who are heedless of their prayer) who are distracted from their prayers and fail to perform them;

translation: Those who delay their Salât (prayer from their stated fixed times).

metadata.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ يُرَآءُونَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Who would be seen (at worship)) who would show off their prayer when they see people praying while abstain from praying when not seen.

translation: Those who do good deeds only to be seen (of men),

metadata.arabic: وَيَمْنَعُونَ ٱلْمَاعُونَ
metadata.Tafsir: (Yet refuse small kindnesses!) i.e. they refuse acts of goodness; and it is also said this means: they refuse the poor-due; and it is also said: they refuse things that are lent and borrowed by people such as cooking pots and utensils, and similar things, which are of benefit to people'.

translation: And prevent Al-Mâ‘ûn (small kindnesses like salt, sugar, water).

metadata.arabic: إِنَّآ أَعْطَيْنَاكَ ٱلْكَوْثَرَ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said about the interpretation of Allah's saying (Lo! We have given thee Abundance): '(Lo! We have given thee Abundance) He says: We have given you, O Muhammad, abundant good and included in this abundant good is the Qur'an; it is also said that Abundance (al-Kawthar) refers to a river in Paradise which was given to Muhammad (pbuh);

translation: Verily, We have granted you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) Al-Kauthar (a river in Paradise).

metadata.arabic: فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَٱنْحَرْ
metadata.Tafsir: (So pray unto thy Lord) in gratitude for that, (and sacrifice) face towards the Qiblah when immolating your sacrifice; it is also said this means: put your right hand on the left hand when in prayer; and it is also said this means: complete your bowing and prostration such that your upper part of the chest is plain; and it is also said that this means: pray to your Lord on the day of immolation and offer a sacrifice.

translation: Therefore turn in prayer to your Lord and sacrifice (to Him only).

metadata.arabic: إِنَّ شَانِئَكَ هُوَ ٱلأَبْتَرُ
metadata.Tafsir: (Lo! It is thy insulter) the one who despises you ((and not thou) who is without posterity) he will be without family, children, wealth or any goodness; he will not be mentioned after his death, i.e. al-'As Ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, while you will be mentioned with every good. This is because, when his son 'Abdullah died, they said: “Muhammad (pbuh) is without posterity”.'

translation: For he who hates you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم), he will be cut off (from posterity and every good thing in this world and in the Hereafter).

metadata.arabic: قُلْ يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلْكَافِرُونَ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (Say: O disbelievers!): '(Say: O disbelievers!) a group of people who derided the Prophet (pbuh) among whom were al-'As Ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi and al-Walid Ibn al-Mughirah, said to the Prophet: “O Muhammad! Surrender to our deity so that we worship the God you worship”. And so Allah said addressing his Prophet: Say, O Muhammad, to these deriders, O disbelievers who mock Allah and the Qur'an.

translation: Say: (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم to these Mushrikûn and Kâfirûn): "O Al-Kafirûn (disbelievers in Allâh, in His Oneness, in His Angels, in His Books, in His Messengers, in the Day of Resurrection, and in Al-Qadar)!

metadata.arabic: لاَ أَعْبُدُ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ
metadata.Tafsir: (I worship not that which ye worship) of idols beside Allah;

translation: "I worship not that which you worship,

metadata.arabic: وَلاَ أَنتُمْ عَابِدُونَ مَآ أَعْبُدُ
metadata.Tafsir: (Nor worship ye that which I worship) that which I will worship in the future.

translation: "Nor will you worship that which I worship.

metadata.arabic: وَلاَ أَنَآ عَابِدٌ مَّا عَبَدتُّمْ
metadata.Tafsir: (And I shall not worship that which ye worship) beside Allah.

translation: "And I shall not worship that which you are worshipping.

metadata.arabic: وَلاَ أَنتُمْ عَابِدُونَ مَآ أَعْبُدُ
metadata.Tafsir: (Nor will ye worship that which I worship) that which I worshipped in the past; it is also said this means: I do not believe in the divinity in which you believe nor will I believe in the divinity which you believe in beside Allah nor will you believe in the divine Oneness of Allah which I believe in.

translation: "Nor will you worship that which I worship.

metadata.arabic: لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ وَلِيَ دِينِ
metadata.Tafsir: (Unto you your religion) of disbelief and ascribing partners to Allah, (and unto me my religion) Islam and faith in Allah. The verses of fighting then abrogated this and the Prophet (pbuh) did fight them'

translation: "To you be your religion, and to me my religion (Islâmic Monotheism)."

metadata.arabic: إِذَا جَآءَ نَصْرُ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلْفَتْحُ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said about the interpretation of Allah's saying (When Allah's succour): '(When Allah's succour) against His enemies, Quraysh as well as others, (and the triumph) and the conquest of Mecca (cometh

translation: When there comes the Help of Allâh (to you, O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم against your enemies) and the conquest (of Makkah).

metadata.arabic: وَرَأَيْتَ ٱلنَّاسَ يَدْخُلُونَ فِي دِينِ ٱللَّهِ أَفْوَاجاً
metadata.Tafsir: And thou seest mankind) the people of Yemen and others (entering the religion of Allah) Islam (in troops) entire groups at a time, when this happens, know that you will die.

translation: And you see that the people enter Allah’s religion (Islâm) in crowds.

metadata.arabic: فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَٱسْتَغْفِرْهُ إِنَّهُ كَانَ تَوَّاباً
metadata.Tafsir: (Then hymn the praises of thy Lord) pray by the command of your Lord in gratitude for this, (and seek forgiveness of Him) from sins. (Lo! He is ever ready to show mercy) and forgiving. The Prophet (pbuh) was therefore informed in this surah that he was to die soon'.

translation: So glorify the Praises of your Lord, and ask His Forgiveness. Verily, He is the One Who accepts the repentance and Who forgives.

metadata.arabic: تَبَّتْ يَدَآ أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (The power of Abu Lahab will perish): '(The power of Abu Lahab will perish) this is because when Allah said to His Prophet (pbuh) (And warn your tribe of near kindred [26: 214]) he called them and said: “Say: there is no god but Allah” and his uncle-the brother of his father from their mother's side-'Abd al-'Uzza whose agnomen was Abu Lahab said: “May you perish! Is this why you summoned us?” Allah then revealed His saying (The power of Abu Lahab will perish) He says: the hand of Abu Lahab is deprived of all good (and he will perish) he lost himself by rejecting belief in Allah's divine Oneness.

translation: Perish the two hands of Abû Lahab (an uncle of the Prophet) and perish he!

metadata.arabic: مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُ وَمَا كَسَبَ
metadata.Tafsir: (His wealth) his abundant wealth (and gains) many children (will not exempt him) in the Hereafter.

translation: His wealth and his children will not benefit him!

metadata.arabic: سَيَصْلَىٰ نَاراً ذَاتَ لَهَبٍ
metadata.Tafsir: (He will be plunged) in the Hereafter (in flaming fire) which will kindle and rage with flames,

translation: He will be burnt in a Fire of blazing flames!

metadata.arabic: وَٱمْرَأَتُهُ حَمَّالَةَ ٱلْحَطَبِ
metadata.Tafsir: (And his wife) Umm Jamilah Bint Harth Ibn Umayyah with him, (the wood carrier) the talebearer who used to go between the Muslims and disbelievers and spread lies among them about each other; it is also said that she used to throw thorns in the way of the mosque whenever she saw the Prophet (pbuh) heading that way.

translation: And his wife, too, who carries wood (thorns of Sa‘dân which she used to put on the way of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, or use to slander him).

metadata.arabic: فِي جِيدِهَا حَبْلٌ مِّن مَّسَدٍ
metadata.Tafsir: (Will have upon her neck a halter of palm fibre) and this halter strangulated her and she died as a result; it is also said that this means: she will have an iron chain on her neck'.

translation: In her neck is a twisted rope of Masad (palm fibre).

metadata.arabic: قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (Say: He is Allah, the One!): '(Say: He is Allah, the One!) the people of Quraysh asked the Prophet (pbuh): “O Muhammad! Describe for us your Lord; is He made of gold or silver?” And so Allah revealed this surah to describe His attributes and traits, saying: say to Quraysh, O Muhammad: He is Allah, the One, He has no son or partner.

translation: Say (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم): "He is Allâh, (the) One.

metadata.arabic: ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ
metadata.Tafsir: (Allah, the eternally Besought of all!) the Master whose glory is at its peak and for Whom all created beings are in need; it is also said that (al-Samad) means: He Who does not eat or drink; it is also said that this means: He Who does not have an interior; it is also said that this means: the Everlasting; and it is also said this means: the Sufficient; and it is also said this means: He who does not have an entrance or exit.

translation: "Allâh-us-Samad (السيد الذي يصمد إليه في الحاجات) [Allâh the Self-Sufficient Master, Whom all creatures need, (He neither eats nor drinks)].

metadata.arabic: لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ
metadata.Tafsir: And it is also said that al-Samad means:(He begetteth not nor was begotten) He says: He did not inherit and will not be inherited; and it is also said this means: He does not have a son who will inherit His dominion and He was not begotten, which means that He did not inherit His dominion.

translation: "He begets not, nor was He begotten.

metadata.arabic: وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَّهُ كُفُواً أَحَدٌ
metadata.Tafsir: (And there is none comparable unto Him) He says: He does not have an opposite, peer, or equal nor anyone who may resemble or begin to resemble Him; and it is also said this means: He does not have any co-equal who would compete with Him about dominion and sovereignty'.

translation: "And there is none co-equal or comparable unto Him."

metadata.arabic: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلْفَلَقِ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of Daybreak): '(Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of Daybreak) He says: Say, O Muhammad, I seek protection, and it is said: I seek refuge, in the Lord of daybreak; and it is also said that al-falaq refers to a well in the Fire; and it is also said that al-falaq is a valley in the Fire.

translation: Say: "I seek refuge with (Allâh), the Lord of the daybreak,

metadata.arabic: مِن شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
metadata.Tafsir: (From the evil of that which He created) from the evil of any from among His creation that possesses evil;

translation: "From the evil of what He has created,

metadata.arabic: وَمِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ
metadata.Tafsir: (From the evil of the darkness when it is intense,

translation: "And from the evil of the darkening (night) as it comes with its darkness; (or the moon as it sets or goes away),

metadata.arabic: وَمِن شَرِّ ٱلنَّفَّاثَاتِ فِي ٱلْعُقَدِ
metadata.Tafsir: And from the evil of malignant witchcraft,

translation: "And from the evil of those who practise witchcraft when they blow in the knots,

metadata.arabic: وَمِن شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ
metadata.Tafsir: And from the evil of the envier when he envieth) this refers to Labid Ibn al-A'sam, the Jew, who was envious of the Prophet (pbuh) and used black magic to separate him from 'A'ishah'.

translation: "And from the evil of the envier when he envies."

metadata.arabic: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلنَّاسِ
metadata.Tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (Say: I seek refuge): '(Say: I seek refuge) and it is also said this means: I seek protection (in the Lord of mankind) in the Lord of the jinn and humankind,

translation: Say: "I seek refuge with (Allâh) the Lord of mankind,

metadata.arabic: مَلِكِ ٱلنَّاسِ
metadata.Tafsir: (The King of mankind) the King of the jinn and humankind,

translation: "The King of mankind -

metadata.arabic: إِلَـٰهِ ٱلنَّاسِ
metadata.Tafsir: (The God of mankind) the Creator of the jinn and humankind,

translation: "The Ilâh (God) of mankind,

metadata.arabic: مِن شَرِّ ٱلْوَسْوَاسِ ٱلْخَنَّاسِ
metadata.Tafsir: (From the evil of the sneaking whisperer) i.e. Satan who runs away and hides himself whenever Allah is mentioned,

translation: "From the evil of the whisperer (devil who whispers evil in the hearts of men) who withdraws (from his whispering in one’s heart after one remembers Allâh).

metadata.arabic: ٱلَّذِى يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ ٱلنَّاسِ
metadata.Tafsir: (Who whispereth in the hearts of mankind) and when Allah is not mentioned, he whispers in the hearts of created beings,

translation: "Who whispers in the breasts of mankind.

metadata.arabic: مِنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ
metadata.Tafsir: (Of the jinn and of mankind) He says: Satan whispers in the hearts of the jinn just as he whispers in the hearts of mankind. The last two surah were revealed about Labid Ibn al-A'sam, the Jew, who used black magic on the Prophet (pbuh) and when the Prophet (pbuh) read these two surahs on Labid's black magic, Allah relieved him from it and it was as if he was untied from his fetters'.

translation: "Of jinn and men."
